safi-cedvel:1-2.t:
* I'rab:
Clause: تلك آيات ... » has no grammatical position; initial (ibtidāʾiyya).

safi-cedvel:3-3.t:
* I'rab:
(نفسك) a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of the active participle باخع, accusative (لا) negative.
And the interpreted maṣdar (ألّا يكونوا ... ) is in the position of a genitive through an omitted preposition, attached to باخع, that is: "because of their lack of belief".
And the clause: «لعلّك باخع ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «يكونوا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أنّ).

* Benefits:
1- ط س م:
The discussion of these letters, which are openers of sūras, has already preceded. To return to what we said:
Are these not three of the letters of the alphabet, namely: ط, س, م? As for the purpose of mentioning them, especially at the beginning of sūras, that is a point of disagreement among the commentators and the linguists, and I still say that the purpose of mentioning these letters may be to draw attention to the value of this language, whether in speech, writing or reading. It is enough for this language that it is the dividing line between man and animal, and enough merit for these letters that they are the weft and warp of the language..!
2- باخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ:
a- باخع is an "active participle", and the active participle works like its verb, whether the verb is intransitive, transitive to one object, or transitive to two objects.
b- The intransitive, as in «خالد مجتهد أولاده» (Khālid, his sons are diligent).
c- The one transitive to one object, as in «هل مكرم سعيد ضيوفه» (Is Saʿīd honouring his guests?). Note: it is not permissible to annex the active participle to its agent, so one does not say: هل مكرم سعيد ضيوفه؟ [Translator's note: the source gives the same example for both the permitted and the impermissible form; translated as written.]
3- Conditions for its working:
a- If it is accompanied by «ال», it needs no other condition, and it works in the past, the present and the future. An example: جاء المعطي المساكين أمس، أو الآن، أو غدا (The one who gives to the poor came yesterday, or now, or tomorrow).
b- If it is not accompanied by «أل», it is required, for it to work, that it be in the sense of the present or future, and that it be preceded by a negation, an interrogative, a noun about which it gives a predicate, a described noun, or a noun for which it is the first (term). Example of the first: ما طالب صديقك رفع الخلاف (Your friend is not demanding the removal of the dispute).
The second: هل عارف أخوك قدر الإنصاف (Does your brother know the worth of fairness?).
The third: خالد مسافر أبواه (Khālid, his parents are travelling).
The fourth: هذا رجل مجتهد أبناؤه (This is a man whose sons are diligent).
The fifth: يخطب علي رافعا صوته (ʿAlī gives a speech raising his voice).
Note: the interrogative and the described noun may be implied:
The first, as in: مقيم سعيد أم منصرف؟ (Is Saʿīd staying or leaving?)
The second, as in the saying of the poet:
كناطح صخرة يوما ليوهنها ... فلم يضرها وأوهى قرنه الوعل
(Like one who butted a rock one day to weaken it; it did not harm it, and the mountain goat weakened its own horn.)

Important note: the intensive forms of the active participle work as it does, and likewise its dual and plural, with the conditions mentioned above.

safi-cedvel:4-6.t:
* I'rab:
(عليهم) attached to (ننزّل), (من السماء) attached to (ننزّل) «[Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of آية.]», (الفاء) a conjunction (لها) attached to the khabar خاضعين.
Clause: «نشأ ... » has no grammatical position; a resumption giving the cause.
And the clause: «ننزّل ... » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a condition, not accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause: «ظلّت أعناقهم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the apodosis clause «[Note: it may be cut off as a resumption, so that it has no position.]».
(5) (الواو) a conjunction (ما) negative (ذكر) genitive in form, nominative in position, the agent of يأتيهم (من الرحمن) attached to an adjective of ذكر «[Note: or attached to محدث, with من in both cases explanatory, or attached to (يأتيهم), with من for the beginning of the range.]» (إلّا) a particle of restriction (عنه) attached to the khabar معرضين.
And the clause: «ما يأتيهم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause إن نشأ.
And the clause: «كانوا عنه معرضين..» is in the position of an accusative; a ḥāl from the pronoun of the absent person, the object.
(6) (الفاء) causal (قد) a particle of affirmation (الفاء) the second one, connecting the apodosis of an implied condition (السين) a particle of the future (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (به) attached to (يستهزئون).
And the clause: «كذّبوا ... » has no grammatical position; giving the cause.
And the clause: «يأتيهم ... » is the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if they deny, then there will come to them ..."
And the clause: «كانوا به يستهزئون» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause: «يستهزئون» is in the position of an accusative; the khabar of كانوا.

* Morphology:
(خاضعين) plural of خاضع, an active participle from the triliteral خضع; its wazn is فاعل and the plural فاعلين.

* Rhetoric:
Difference in conjunction: in His saying, the Exalted, فَظَلَّتْ أَعْناقُهُمْ لَها خاضِعِينَ.
His saying, the Exalted, فظلّت is conjoined to the consequence, which is ننزل, because if it had been said أنزلنا it would have been correct, and perhaps it is what the context requires. But it was made different because in conjoining the past to the future there is an indication of its certainty and that it will surely come to be, since the past verb indicates that the action has taken place and is definite. It has parallels in the Qur'an that will come in their places.
Rational figurative usage (al-majāz al-ʿaqlī): in His saying, the Exalted, أَعْناقُهُمْ لَها خاضِعِينَ.
It may be asked how خاضعين could come as a khabar of الأعناق, when submission is among the characteristics of rational beings, while the original wording would have been «فظلوا لها خاضعين». The secret in this is that, since they were described with submission, which belongs to rational beings, it was said خاضعين, as preceded in His saying, the Exalted, لِي ساجِدِينَ

safi-cedvel:7-9.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for a rebuking question (الواو) a conjunction «[Note: it conjoins the verb to an implied resumption, so nothing prevents making it resumptive.]», (إلى الأرض) attached to (يروا), that is, "they look" (كم) a khabariyya (declarative) كم, a metonym for a number, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, a fronted direct object (mafʿūl bihi) (فيها) attached to (أنبتنا), (من كلّ) the tamyīz (specification) of كم..
Clause: «يروا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied resumption, that is "Did they deny and not see ..."
And the clause: «أنبتنا ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption «[Note: or in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from الأرض.]».
(8) (في ذلك) attached to an omitted khabar of inna (اللام) of initiation, giving emphasis (آية) the ism of inna, accusative (الواو) parenthetical – or circumstantial (ḥāliyya) – (ما) negative.
And the clause: إنّ في ذلك لآية has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «ما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين ... » has no grammatical position; parenthetical – or a ḥāl from the agent of يروا.
(9) (الواو) a conjunction (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis (الرحيم) a second khabar, nominative.
And the clause: «إنّ ربّك ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause إنّ في ذلك.
And the clause: «هو العزيز ... » is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of inna.

safi-cedvel:10-11.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (إذ) a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر ("remember") (أن) explicative «[Note: it was preceded by a verb that contains the meaning of saying without its letters, namely (نادى) ... and it may be a maṣdar particle, and the interpreted maṣdar (أن أئت) is in the position of a genitive through an omitted preposition, attached to (نادي), that is بأن أئت.]» ...
Clause: «نادى ربّك ... » is in the position of a genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «ائت ... » has no grammatical position; explicative ...
(11) (قوم) a badal (substitute) for القوم, accusative like it (ألا) a particle of offering containing the meaning of wonder ...
And the clause: «يتّقون ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.

safi-cedvel:12-14.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) a vocative, a muḍāf, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the implied fatḥa on what precedes the yāʾ, which was dropped for lightness ... and the dropped yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and the nūn mentioned in (يكذّبون) is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), which came before the dropped yāʾ to suit the verse ending.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the vocative clause ... is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech «[Note: it may be parenthetical, of supplication seeking mercy, and the clause إنّي أخاف becomes the content of speech.]».
And the clause: «إنّي أخاف ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the vocative.
And the clause: is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of inna.
And the clause: «أخاف» is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of inna.
And the clause: «يكذّبون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the interpreted maṣdar «أن يكذّبون» is in the position of an accusative, a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) whose governor is أخاف.
(13) (الواو) a conjunction – or resumptive – and the second is a conjunction only (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition «[Note: because it contains the meaning of causation.]», (إلى هارون) attached to (أرسل), and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa, it being a diptote.
And the clause: «يضيق صدري..» is in the position of a nominative; conjoined to the clause أخاف «[Note: or it is resumptive within the scope of the saying and so has no position.]».
And the clause: «لا ينطلق لساني..» is in the position of a nominative; conjoined to the clause يضيق صدري.
And the clause: «أرسل إلى هارون ... » is in the position of a jussive; the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if I become a messenger, then send ..."
(14) (الواو) resumptive (لهم) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذنب), (عليّ) attached to the omitted khabar (الفاء) a conjunction «[Note: or connecting the apodosis of an implied condition because it contains the meaning of causation.]», (أن يقتلون) like أن يكذّبون ...
And the clause: «لهم عليّ ذنب ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive within the scope of the saying.
And the clause: «أخاف ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause لهم عليّ ذنب «[Note: or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "أنا", and the nominal clause is the apodosis of the implied condition, that is: "if I go to them, then I fear that they will kill me."]».
And the clause: «يقتلون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يقتلون) is in the position of an accusative, a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) whose governor is أخاف.

safi-cedvel:15-17.t:
* I'rab:
The agent of (قال) is a pronoun that refers to Allah (كلّا) a particle of rebuke and deterrence (الفاء) a conjunction (بآياتنا) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of اذهبا, that is, "accompanied by Our signs" (معكم) an adverbial, accusative, attached to (مستمعون), «[Note: the speech was put in the plural for magnification.]».
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption ... and the content of speech is implied, indicated by the particle of deterrence, that is: "desist from fear ..."
And the clause: «اذهبا ... » is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the implied clause of the content of speech.
And the clause: «إنّا معكم مستمعون ... » has no grammatical position; giving the cause ...
(16) (الفاء) a conjunction in both places, (رسول) the khabar of inna, and it has been put in the singular because it is among the words in which the singular, the dual and the plural are alike, like الطفل and الضيف «[Note: or because each one of us is a messenger to you.]».
And the clause: «ائتيا ... » is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause اذهبا..
And the clause: «قولا ... » is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause ائتيا.
And the clause: «إنّا رسول ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
(17) (أن) a particle of explanation «[Note: because of the meaning of saying, without its letters, in the word (رسول); and it may be a maṣdar particle, with the interpreted maṣdar in the position of a genitive through an omitted bāʾ, attached to رسول.]», (معنا) an adverbial, accusative, attached to (أرسل), (بني) a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ, so it is attached to the sound masculine plural.
And the clause: «أرسل ... » has no grammatical position; explicative..

* Morphology:
(مستمعون) plural of مستمع, an active participle from the quinqueliteral استمع; its wazn is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative usage (majāz): in His saying, the Exalted, إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُسْتَمِعُونَ – listening (istimāʿ) in regard to Him, the Mighty and Majestic, is a figure for hearing (samʿ), chosen for emphasis, because it carries an acknowledgement of perception, which is among the things Allah the Exalted is above, whether by a sense organ or not.
Some of them said: «إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُسْتَمِعُونَ» is a whole sentence of representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya): the Glorified likened His state, the Mighty and Majestic, to the state of one of might who has attended the disputation of a people, listening to what goes on between them, in order to support his allies and make them prevail over their enemies, as an emphasis of the promise of help.

* Benefits:
- كلّا:
Sībawayh said: «As for كلّا, it is rebuke and deterrence»; it has no meaning for them other than that.
The closest thing that can be said of it is what Ibn Fāris says:
Indeed كلّا occurs in the usage of speech in four ways: rejection, deterrence, an introduction to an oath, and the opening of speech with it like «ألا». In the Noble Qur'an there are examples of these four categories, so do not hurry..!
- The word «رسول»:
It may be an attribute for the singular, the dual and the plural, like the maṣdars, so that it has even been said that «الرسول» means الرسالة (the message), and therefore it is counted among the maṣdars. And Allah knows best...!

safi-cedvel:18-19.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for an affirmative question (istifhām taqrīrī) «[Note: or a rebuking one.]», and the sign of the jussive in (نربّك) is the dropping of the weak letter (فينا) attached to the verb نربك, with an omitted muḍāf, that is "in our dwellings" (وليدا) an accusative ḥāl from the pronoun of the addressee (الواو) a conjunction (فينا) the second, attached to (لبثت), with an omitted muḍāf likewise (من عمرك) attached to a ḥāl of سنين – an adjective put before the noun it describes – (سنين) an adverb of time, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ, attached to the masculine plural, attached to (لبثت).
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «نربّك» is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: «لبثت ... » is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause of the content of speech.
(19) (الواو) a conjunction (التي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, an adjective of فعلتك (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) (من الكافرين) the khabar of أنت.
And the clause: «فعلت ... » is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause of the content of speech.
And the clause: «فعلت (the second) » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (التي).
And the clause: «أنت من الكافرين» is in the position of an accusative; a ḥāl from the agent of فعلت.

* Morphology:
(نربّك) it has ʾiʿlāl by dropping, to suit the jussive, and its origin is نربيّك; its wazn is نفعّك.
(وليدا) a derived adjective from the triliteral ولد in the passive; its wazn is فعيل in the sense of مفعول.
(فعلتك) a maṣdar of single occurrence (maṣdar marra) of فعل; its wazn is the same as its form, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
Vagueness (ibhām): in His saying, the Exalted, وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ الَّتِي فَعَلْتَ.
- He enumerated His favour upon him from that, and rebuked him for what had happened at his hands of killing his baker, and made it appear dreadful to him with His saying «وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ». A way in which it is made dreadful to him is that bringing it in summary and vague form is an announcement that, because of its dreadfulness, it is not uttered except by allusion. A parallel in the magnification gained from vagueness is His saying «فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِنَ الْيَمِّ ما غَشِيَهُمْ». And there are many like it.
فعلتك is a «maṣdar of a single occurrence» or maṣdar of number, which is mentioned to show the number of the action.
a- It is built from the bare triliteral on the pattern «فعلة» with fatḥa on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn. Like وقفت وقفة ووقفتين ووقفات.
b- If the verb has more than three letters, we add the tāʾ to its maṣdar, like «أكرمته إكرامة وتدحرج تدحرجة».
c- If its maṣdar ends in tāʾ, then a word is mentioned that indicates its number:
Like: رحمته رحمة واحدة.
Note: if a verb with more than three letters has two maṣdars, one better known than the other, the maṣdar of single occurrence is built on the better known of its two maṣdars, so you say: زلزلته زلزلة واحدة and قاتلته مقاتلة واحدة, and you do not say زلزالة nor قتالة.

safi-cedvel:20-22.t:
* I'rab:
- (إذا) – with tanwīn – a particle of response having no effect (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) (من الضالّين) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أنا. «[Note: من الضالّين means "of the ignorant"; Ibn Jarīr said: the Arabs put ḍalāl (going astray) in the place of jahl (ignorance).]»
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «فعلتها ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: «أنا من الضالّين» is in the position of an accusative; a ḥāl from the agent of فعلتها.
(21) (الفاء) a conjunction in both places (منكم) attached to (فررت), (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the meaning of a condition, attached to the implied apodosis (لي) attached to an omitted second object (mafʿūl bihi) whose governor is وهب (من المرسلين) attached to the second object of (جعلني).
And the clause: «فررت ... » is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause فعلتها.
And the clause: «خفتكم ... » is in the position of a genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
And the clause: «وهب ... ربّي» is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause فررت.
And the clause: «جعلني ... » is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause وهب.
(22) (الواو) a conjunction (تلك) a demonstrative, a mubtadaʾ «[Note: al-Akhfash mentioned that there is an implied interrogative hamza here, giving rebuke, that is: "Is that a favour ...?" because the enslaving of the Children of Israel is not a favour.]», its khabar is نعمة (عليّ) attached to (تمنّها), (أن) a maṣdar particle.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن عبّدت..) is in the position of a nominative, an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of the mubtadaʾ (تلك) «[Note: or it is a badal of the hāʾ in (تمنّها), or it is in the position of a genitive through an implied bāʾ, or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي" ...]».
(بني) a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ, so it is attached to the sound masculine plural.
And the clause: «تلك نعمة ... » is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause of the content of speech «[Note: or it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.]».
And the clause: «تمنّها ... » is in the position of a nominative; an adjective of نعمة.
And the clause: «عبّدت..» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).

safi-cedvel:23-23.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (ربّ).
Clause: «قال فرعون ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «ما ربّ العالمين» is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to an implied clause that is the content of speech, that is: "Is there a god other than me, and what is the Lord of the worlds ..."

safi-cedvel:24-24.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو" (ما) a relative noun in the position of a genitive, conjoined to السموات (بينهما) an adverbial, accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila of ما (كنتم) an incomplete past verb, indeclinable, in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and تم is the ism of كان.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «هو» ربّ» .. is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: «إن كنتم موقنين..» has no grammatical position; resumptive within the scope of the saying ... and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, its implied form being: "then believe in Him alone" «[Note: or "this is more fitting for certainty because of its clarity."]».

safi-cedvel:25-25.t:
* I'rab:
(لمن) attached to (قال), (حوله) an adverbial, accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila of من (ألّا) a particle of offering, for expressing wonder.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «تستمعون..» is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّكم) the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو" (ربّ) conjoined with the wāw to ربّكم, nominative..
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «هو» ربّكم» is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.

* Rhetoric:
The general and the particular: in His saying, the Exalted, قالَ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ.
By mentioning the heavens and the earth and what is between them He encompassed all creatures; then He mentioned them and then their fathers, and mentioned the East and the West. So He first generalised, and then particularised from the general, to point to themselves and their fathers, because the nearest thing for a rational being to look into is himself and those who were born of him, and what he has witnessed and seen of the proofs of the Maker, and of the one who moves from one form to another and from one state to another from the time of his birth to the time of his death. Then He particularised the East and the West, because the rising of the sun from one of the two horizons and its setting in the other, according to a regular measure through the seasons of the year and an even reckoning, is among the clearest things used as evidence; and because of its clarity, Khalīl Allah (Abraham) moved to arguing with it, away from arguing with giving life and death, against Nimrod son of Canaan, and "the one who disbelieved was confounded."

safi-cedvel:27-27.t:
* I'rab:
(الذي) a relative noun in the position of an accusative, an adjective of رسولكم, and the deputy agent of the verb (أرسل) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو", and it is the returning pronoun (إليكم) attached to (أرسل), (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis ...
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «إنّ رسولكم ... لمجنون» is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: «أرسل إليكم ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).

safi-cedvel:28-28.t:
* I'rab:
The i'rab of its like – words and clauses – has already preceded «[Note: in verse (24) of this sūra.]».
And the clause: «تعقلون ... » is in the position of an accusative; the khabar of كنتم.

safi-cedvel:29-29.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) preparing for the oath (إن) a jussive conditional particle (اتّخذت) a past verb, indeclinable, in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) (إلها) a first object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative, and (غيري) a second object, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the implied fatḥa on what precedes the yāʾ.. and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (اللام) the second is the lām of the oath (أجعلنّك) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of a nominative.. and the kāf is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) (من المسجونين) attached to an omitted second object whose governor is أجعلنّك.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «إن اتّخذت ... » is in the position of an accusative [Translator's note: the source reads "لا محلّ نصب"; the sense is "in the position of an accusative"]; the content of speech.
And the clause: «أجعلنّك ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath ...
And the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.

* Morphology:
(المسجونين) plural of المسجون, a passive participle from the triliteral (سجن); its wazn is مفعول.

safi-cedvel:30-30.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for a question (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle (بشيء) attached to (جئتك).
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «جئتك ... » is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl, and the governor is implied, namely the content of speech, that is: "Will you do that to me while I have come with something that shows the truth of my claim ...?"
And the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what preceded.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition (به) attached to (ائت), (من الصادقين) the khabar of كنت.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «ائت به ... » is the apodosis of an implied condition, that is, in the position of a jussive: "if you are truthful, then bring it ..." And the clause of the condition is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: «كنت من الصادقين ... » has no grammatical position; explicative ...
And the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, that is: "then bring it.."

safi-cedvel:32-33.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive, and the agent of (ألقى) is a pronoun that refers to Mūsā, peace be upon him (الفاء) a conjunction (إذا) a particle of suddenness (مبين) an adjective of ثعبان, nominative.
Clause: «ألقى عصاه ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «هي ثعبان ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
(33) (الواو) a conjunction (للناظرين) attached to an omitted second khabar of the mubtadaʾ هي, that is "dazzling" «[Note: the khabar came as a specific being (kawn khāṣṣ) because it confirms the meaning of the first khabar.]».
And the clause: «نزع ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «هي بيضاء ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause نزع.

* Benefits:
The إذا of suddenness:
It has been mentioned that «إذا» can be explicative, adverbial or of suddenness.
Here we wish to stress إذا of suddenness.
a- It is specific to nominal clauses, it does not need a response, it does not occur at the beginning of speech, its meaning is the ḥāl (the present state), and the more probable view is that it is a particle, as in His saying, the Exalted: فَأَلْقاها فَإِذا هِيَ حَيَّةٌ تَسْعى.
And His saying in the verse we are dealing with «فَأَلْقى عَصاهُ فَإِذا هِيَ ثُعْبانٌ مُبِينٌ» «وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُ فَإِذا هِيَ بَيْضاءُ لِلنَّاظِرِينَ» .
b- It is also a response to a conditional consequence, like the fāʾ. Allah the Exalted said: وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِذا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ.
c- It may take the place of the khabar, as in «جئتك فإذا أخوك» – "the implied form: جئتك فإذا أخوك موجود" (I came to you and, lo, your brother is present).

safi-cedvel:34-35.t:
* I'rab:
(للملأ) attached to (قال) (حوله) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to a ḥāl of الملأ (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «إنّ هذا لساحر ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
(35) (من أرضكم) attached to (يخرجكم), (بسحره) attached to (يخرجكم), the bāʾ being causal (الفاء) a conjunction (ماذا) an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative, a fronted direct object (mafʿūl bihi) «[Note: or (ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and (ذا) a relative noun, a khabar, and the clause (ماذا ... ) is resumptive, and the returning pronoun of the relative is omitted, that is "you command with it", and the clause تأمرون is the ṣila of the relative.]».
And the clause: «يريد ... » is in the position of a nominative; an adjective of ساحر «[Note: it may be in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from ساحر because it is a description.]».
And the clause: يخرجكم ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يخرجكم) is in the position of an accusative, a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) whose governor is يريد.
And the clause: «تأمرون» is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause of the content of speech.

safi-cedvel:36-37.t:
* I'rab:
(أرجه) an imperative verb and the hāʾ is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) (أخاه) conjoined with the wāw to the hāʾ, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the alif, and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi (في المدائن) attached to (ابعث) by including in it the meaning of انشر (spread).
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «أرجه ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: «ابعث ... » is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause أرجه.
(37) (بكلّ) attached to (يأتوك), which is jussive as the response to a request, and the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the nūn.
And the clause: «يأتوك ... » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of an implied condition, not accompanied by the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:38-40.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) a conjunction (لميقات) attached to جمع (معلوم) an adjective of يوم, genitive.
Clause: «جمع السحرة» has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied resumed clause, that is: "so he sent the gatherers, so the magicians were gathered."
(39) (الواو) a conjunction (للناس) attached to (قيل), (هل) a particle of question containing the meaning of urging, and the hope in (لعلّنا) is for the meaning of desire for not following Mūsā (كانوا) an incomplete past verb, in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) (هم) a separation pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) «[Note: or a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative, emphasis for the attached pronoun in (كانوا).]».
And the clause: «قيل ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause جمع السحرة.
And the clause: «هل أنتم مجتمعون» is in the position of a nominative; the deputy agent (nāʾib al-fāʿil).
And the clause: «لعلّنا نتّبع ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «نتّبع ... » is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of لعلّنا.
And the clause: «كانوا ... الغالبين» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption ... and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

* Morphology:
(مجتمعون) plural of مجتمع, an active participle from the quinqueliteral اجتمع; its wazn is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:41-41.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) a conjunction (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the meaning of a condition, attached to (قالوا), (لفرعون) attached to (قالوا) (الهمزة) for a question (لنا) attached to an omitted khabar of inna (اللام) the lām of initiation, for emphasis (أجرا) the ism of inna, accusative (كنّا) an incomplete past verb, indeclinable, in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) (نحن) a separation pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) «[Note: or a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative, emphasis for the attached pronoun in (كنّا).]», (الغالبين) the khabar of كنّا, accusative.
Clause: «جاء السحرة..» is in the position of a genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «إنّ لنا لأجرا ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: إن كنّا ... الغالبين ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

safi-cedvel:42-42.t:
* I'rab:
(نعم) a particle of response having no effect (الواو) a conjunction (إذا) a particle of response (اللام) for emphasis (من المقرّبين) the khabar of inna.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «إنكم لمن المقرّبين ... » is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the implied clause of the content of speech, which is indicated by the response particle نعم, that is: "You will have a reward, and you will be among those brought near."

safi-cedvel:43-43.t:
* I'rab:
(لهم) attached to (قال), (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), and the returning pronoun is omitted, that is "ones who cast it".
And the clause: «قال لهم موسى ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «ألقوا ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: «أنتم ملقون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).

safi-cedvel:44-48.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) a conjunction, and likewise (الواو) , (بعزة) attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being نقسم ("we swear") (اللام) for emphasis.
Clause: ألقوا ... has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause قال لهم موسى «[Note: in the preceding verse.]».
And the clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause ألقوا «[Note: it may be circumstantial (ḥāliyya) with an implied (قد), in which case it is in the position of an accusative.]».
And the clause: « (نقسم) بعزّة فرعون» is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: «إنا لنحن الغالبون» has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath.
And the clause: «نحن الغالبون» is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of inna.
(45) (الفاء) a conjunction in both places (إذا هي) its i'rab has preceded «[Note: in verse (32) of this sūra.]», (ما) a relative, a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), and the returning pronoun is omitted, that is "what they fabricate".
And the clause: «ألقى موسى ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause ألقوا ...
And the clause: «هي تلقف ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause ألقى.
And the clause: «تلقف ... » is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هي).
And the clause: «يأفكون» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
(46) (الفاء) a conjunction (السحرة) the deputy agent of the verb (ألقي) (ساجدين) an accusative ḥāl from السحرة, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
And the clause: «ألقي السحرة ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause ألقى موسى ...
(47-48) (بربّ) attached to (آمنّا) ... (ربّ) a badal (substitute) for the first ربّ, genitive «[Note: or an ʿaṭf bayān, because the wording (ربّ موسى) is more explicit and clearer than the wording (ربّ العالمين), since Pharaoh had claimed lordship, so if they had confined themselves to it, it would not have been explicit about the true Lord, Glory be to Him ... Ibn Hishām said it.]».
And the clause: «قالوا ... » is in the position of an accusative; a ḥāl from السحرة with an implied (قد) «[Note: or it is an explanatory resumption having no position.]» and the clause: «آمنّا ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.

* Rhetoric:
Derivative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tabaʿiyya): in His saying, the Exalted, فَأُلْقِيَ السَّحَرَةُ ساجِدِينَ.
He expressed the falling down by "casting" (ilqāʾ), because it was mentioned along with the castings (of the magicians), so the way of mushākala (verbal harmony) was followed. And in it also, along with observing the harmony, is that when they saw what they saw they could not help but throw themselves to the ground in prostration, as if they had been seized and flung down. So there is a derivative metaphor whose beauty was increased by the harmony.

safi-cedvel:49-49.t:
* I'rab:
(له) attached to (آمنتم) by including in it the meaning of استسلمتم وانقدتم (you submitted and yielded) (قبل) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (آمنتم) (لكم) attached to (آذن).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن آذن) is in the position of a genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
(اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis (الذي) a relative noun in the position of a nominative, an adjective of كبيركم (الفاء) a conjunction (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (سوف) a particle of the future (من خلاف) attached to a ḥāl of الأيدي والأرجل (أجمعين) an accusative ḥāl «[Note: or emphasis (tawkīd) for the accusative pronoun of the addressee.]».
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «آمنتم له ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: «آذن لكم ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «إنّه لكبيركم ... » has no grammatical position; giving the cause..
And the clause: «علّمكم ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «لسوف تعلمون ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath ...
And the implied oath clause is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause of the content of speech.
And the clause: «أقطّعنّ ... » has no grammatical position; an ʿaṭf bayān of the clause تعلمون.
And the clause: «أصلّبنّكم ... » has no grammatical position; an ʿaṭf nasaq (conjunction) to the clause أقطّعنّ.

safi-cedvel:50-51.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) the lā of generic negation (ضير) the ism of لا, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (إلى ربّنا) attached to (منقلبون), and the khabar of لا is omitted, its implied form being: "upon us" – or "in that".
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «لا ضير ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: «إنّا ... منقلبون» has no grammatical position; giving the cause.
(51) (أن) a maṣdar and accusative particle (لنا) attached to (يغفر), (أن) a maṣdar particle ...
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يغفر ... ) is in the position of a genitive through an omitted bāʾ, attached to (نطمع), that is بأن يغفر.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن كنّا ... ) is in the position of a genitive through an omitted lām, attached to (يغفر), that is لأن كنّا ...
And the clause: «إنّا نطمع ... » has no grammatical position; a second explanation of cause or a badal of the clause of the explanation of cause.
And the clause: «نطمع ... » is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of inna.
And the clause: «يغفر ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «كنّا أوّل المؤمنين» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the second particle-type relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(ضير) a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb ضاره الأمر يضيره, pattern of ضرب, that is "it harmed him"; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa followed by sukūn.

* Benefits:
- لا ضير «the lā of generic negation»:
a- The divisions of its ism and their rulings:
Its ism is divided into three kinds: singular (mufrad), muḍāf, and resembling the muḍāf.
1- The singular: as in His saying, the Exalted, ذلِكَ الْكِتابُ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ. Its ruling: it is built on what it would take in the accusative, «fatḥa, yāʾ or kasra», as in: «لا رجل في الدار ولا رجال فيها، ولا رجلين عندنا، ولا مذمومين في المدرسة، ولا مذمومات محبوبات» (No man is in the house, nor men in it; no two men with us; no blameworthy ones in the school; no blameworthy, beloved women). It is also permissible to build the sound feminine plural on the fatḥa.
2- The muḍāf: it is declinable, accusative.
3- The one resembling the muḍāf: its ruling is also to be declinable, accusative.
Note: the omission of its ism is rare, as in «لا عليك» that is لا بأس عليك (no harm upon you), and the omission of its khabar is frequent when it is known, as in «لا بأس» (no harm) and His saying, the Exalted: قالُوا لا ضَيْرَ إِنَّا إِلى رَبِّنا مُنْقَلِبُونَ that is, لا ضير علينا (no harm upon us), and likewise this verse that is before us.

safi-cedvel:52-52.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (إلى موسى) attached to (أوحينا), (أن) explicative «[Note: or a maṣdar particle, and the interpreted maṣdar (أن أسر) is in the position of a genitive through an omitted preposition, attached to (أوحينا), that is بأن أسر.]», (أسر) an imperative verb, indeclinable by the dropping of the weak letter, and the agent is "you" (بعبادي) attached to (أسر), and the bāʾ is for accompaniment.
Clause: «أوحينا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «أسر ... » has no grammatical position; explicative.
And the clause: «إنّكم متّبعون ... » has no grammatical position; giving the cause.

* Morphology:
(متّبعون) plural of متّبع, a passive participle from the quinqueliteral اتّبع; its wazn is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:53-56.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (في المدائن) attached to (أرسل) by including in it the meaning of بثّ or نشر (spread) (حاشرين) a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
Clause: «أرسل فرعون ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
(54) (اللام) for emphasis (قليلون) an adjective of شرذمة, following it in its meaning.
And the clause: إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ لَشِرْذِمَةٌ ... is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech of an implied "saying", and the implied one is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from Pharaoh, that is: "he sent, saying: Indeed these ..."
(55) (لنا) attached to (غائظون) «[Note: or the (اللام) is a redundant one of reinforcement, and the pronoun of the speaker is in the position of an accusative, a direct object of the active participle غائظون.]», (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis.
And the clause: «إنّهم لنا لغائظون» is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause إنّ هؤلاء ...
(56) (لجميع) like لشرذمة (حاذرون) an adjective of جميع, nominative «[Note: or a second khabar of inna, nominative.]».
And the clause: «إنّا لجميع ... » is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause إنّ هؤلاء ...

* Morphology:
(54) شرذمة: a noun meaning "group"; its wazn is فعللة with kasra on the fāʾ and on the first lām and sukūn on the ʿayn.
(55) غائطون: [Translator's note: the source writes غائطون (with ṭāʾ) here, though the Qur'anic word is غائظون (with ẓāʾ), as given in the i'rab section above and in the verse; translated as written.] plural of غائظ, an active participle of غاظه, that is "he angered him", pattern of ضرب; its wazn is فاعل.
(56) جميع: the word came here in the sense of "group", "assembly" or "people", a collective noun (ism jamʿ) with no singular from its form; its wazn is فعيل.
(حاذرون) plural of حاذر, an active participle from the triliteral (حذر), pattern of فرح, meaning "prepared and ready"; on the pattern فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying, the Exalted, إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ لَشِرْذِمَةٌ قَلِيلُونَ.
The shirdhima is a group or a small assembly. It would have been possible to suffice with it as an expression of fewness, but he described it as "few, very few", to add to their disdain and to belittle their standing.
He thus made them few in four ways: he referred to them as الشرذمة, which indicates fewness; then he described them as few; then he put their description in the plural so as to show that every kind of them is few; and he chose the sound plural to indicate fewness. And there is another way of making them few, a fifth: that putting the description in the plural while the described noun is singular may be an emphasis on the attachment of that description to the described and its utmost degree in it relative to other things described by it, as they say: "Zayd and I are hungry (jiyāʿ)", as an emphasis on describing him with hunger. So likewise here he made قليلا plural when the basic form was to make it singular, so that it would be said: لشرذمة قليلة, as it was singular in His saying «كَمْ مِنْ فِئَةٍ قَلِيلَةٍ». so that by putting it in the plural it would indicate their extreme fewness.
[Translator's note: the source's example reads "معا زيد جياع", which appears garbled; translated as "Zayd and I are hungry" as the likely sense.]

safi-cedvel:57-58.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (من جنّات) attached to (أخرجناهم) ..
And the clause: «أخرجناهم..» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

safi-cedvel:59-60.t:
* I'rab:
(كذلك) attached to the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is "Our bringing them out was thus" (الواو) a conjunction (بني) a second object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ, so it is attached to the masculine plural.
Clause: « (إخراجنا) كذلك ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «أورثناها ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive.
(60) (الفاء) a conjunction (مشرقين) an accusative ḥāl from the agent of أتبعوهم.
And the clause: «أتبعوهم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied resumed clause, that is: "so they gathered, so they pursued them".

safi-cedvel:61-61.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the meaning of a condition, attached to the response قال (اللام) for emphasis.
Clause: «تراءى الجمعان ... » is in the position of a genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «قال أصحاب ... » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «إنّا لمدركون ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.

* Morphology:
(تراءى) it has ʾiʿlāl by substitution; its origin is تراءي – with a yāʾ at its end – the yāʾ was voweled after a fatḥa so it turned into alif, and it is written in the form of the undotted yāʾ because it is beyond the fourth letter.
(مدركون) plural of مدرك, a passive participle from the quadriliteral أدرك; its wazn is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:62-62.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) a particle of rebuke and deterrence (معي) an adverbial, accusative, attached to an omitted khabar of inna (ربّي) the ism of inna, and the sign of the accusative in both words (معي، ربّي) is the implied fatḥa on what precedes the yāʾ (السين) a particle of the future, and the (النون) in (سيهدين) is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), which came before the dropped yāʾ of the speaker to suit the verse ending.
Clause: «قال..» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «إنّ معي ربّي ... » has no grammatical position; giving the cause of the implied content of speech, that is: "Never! They will not overtake us."
And the clause: «سيهدين» is in the position of a nominative; a second khabar of the particle resembling a verb «[Note: or it is the sole khabar, and the adverbial before it (معي) is attached to a ḥāl from ربّي ... it may be that the clause is a ḥāl from ربّي, and the governor in the ḥāl is the meaning of emphasis in inna.]».

safi-cedvel:63-68.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (إلى موسى) attached to (أوحينا), (أن) explicative «[Note: it was preceded by a verb that contains the meaning of saying without its letters, namely أوحينا.. and the particle may be a maṣdar particle, with the interpreted maṣdar in the position of a genitive through an omitted preposition, attached to (أوحينا), that is بأن اضرب.]», (بعصاك) attached to the verb اضرب, and the (الباء) is for seeking aid (الفاء) a conjunction in both places (كالطود) attached to an omitted khabar of كان.
Clause: «أوحينا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «اضرب ... » has no grammatical position; explicative.
And the clause: «انفلق ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied clause, that is: "so he struck, so it split".
And the clause: «كان كلّ فرق ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause انفلق.
(64) (الواو) a conjunction (ثمّ) an adverb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of an accusative, attached to (أزلفنا).
And the clause: «أزلفنا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أوحينا.
(65) (الواو) a conjunction in both places (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, conjoined to موسى (معه) an adverbial, accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila of من (أجمعين) an accusative ḥāl from موسى وقومه «[Note: or a semantic emphasis (tawkīd maʿnawī) for موسى وقومه, accusative.]», and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
And the clause: «أنجينا» ... has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أنجينا. [Translator's note: the source reads thus; the clause label appears to be a slip, since a clause cannot be conjoined to itself.]
(66) (ثم) a conjunction.
And the clause: أغرقنا has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أنجينا.
(67) في ذلك) attached to the khabar of inna (اللام) for emphasis (آية) the ism of inna, postponed, accusative (الواو) parenthetical (ما) negative.
And the clause: «إنّ في ذلك لآية ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «ما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين.» has no grammatical position; parenthetical.
(68) (الواو) a conjunction (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis (الرحيم) a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ هو.
And the clause: «إنّ ربك لهو ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause إنّ في ذلك ...
And the clause: «هو العزيز ... » is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(63) فرق: a noun meaning "group" or "that which is split from something"; its wazn is فعل with kasra followed by sukūn.
(الطود) a non-derived noun (ism jāmid) denoting a thing, for a huge mountain; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa followed by sukūn; its plural is أطواد.

* Benefits:
1- «The redundant bāʾ in the khabar of ليس and كان»: ليس and كان are specific in permitting the bāʾ to be added redundantly to the khabar of each, and its addition is frequent in the khabar of ليس and in the khabar of the Hijazi ما; as for كان, it is not added to its khabar unless negation or prohibition precedes it, as in the saying of al-Shanfarā:
وإن مدّت الأيدي إلى الزاد لم أكن ... بأعجلهم إذا جشع القوم أعجل
(And if hands are stretched out to the provisions, I am not the hastiest of them when the people are greedy and hasten.)
2- A description of Egypt:
When ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ was established in the governorship of Egypt, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to him: "Describe Egypt to me." So he wrote to him:
«The letter of the Commander of the Faithful – may Allah prolong his life – has arrived, asking me about Egypt:
Know, O Commander of the Faithful, that Egypt is a dusty-coloured village and a green tree; its length is a month and its width ten (days); a dusty mountain and a dun-coloured sand enclose it; through its middle strides a Nile, blessed in its mornings and auspicious in its evenings, in which rising and falling run like the running of the sun and the moon. It has a season in which its milk flows abundantly and its flies multiply; it is fed by the springs and fountains of the earth, until, when its dust grows thick and its waves grow great, it overflows its two banks, so it is not possible to get from one village to another except in small boats, light skiffs and little craft that look, in the visions, like the leaves of the evening. Then, when it has completed its rise, it turns back on its heels, as at the first when it began its course, and it swells in its reaching (its fullness). Then there come out the people of a despised community and a guarded covenant, who plough the land and sow the grain in it, hoping thereby for growth from the Lord, for others than those who heard of their toil, so it is gained from them without their effort. Then, when the crop surrounds (the fields) and shines, the dew waters it and it is nourished from beneath the soil. So while Egypt, O Commander of the Faithful, is a white pearl, behold it is black ambergris; then behold it is a green emerald; then behold it is a variegated brocade. So blessed be Allah, the Creator of what He wills» – to the end of that delightful letter.
Al-Maqrīzī explained the obscure points of this letter in his Khiṭaṭ, with a full and useful explanation. Whoever wishes may return to it in its proper places in the longer works.
[Translator's note: the translation of the letter follows the wording of the source; some rare words in it are obscure and the rendering of them is tentative.]

safi-cedvel:69-70.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive «[Note: the i'rab scholars make it a conjunction, conjoining the clause (اتل) to the implied clause to which (إذ) is attached in His saying: إذ نادى ربّك موسى ... verse (10), and in this there is some affectation.]» (عليهم) attached to (اتل), (إذ) an adverb of past time, in the position of an accusative, a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) for نبأ «[Note: or attached to the maṣdar نبأ.]» (لأبيه) attached to (قال), (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, a fronted direct object (mafʿūl bihi) whose governor is (تعبدون).
Clause: «اتل ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «قال ... » is in the position of a genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «تعبدون ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.

safi-cedvel:71-71.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) a conjunction (لها) attached to the khabar عاكفين.
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «نعبد ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: «نظل لها عاكفين..» is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause نعبد.

* Rhetoric:
Elaboration (iṭnāb): in His saying, the Exalted, قالُوا نَعْبُدُ أَصْناماً فَنَظَلُّ لَها عاكِفِينَ.
His saying, the Exalted, «ما تَعْبُدُونَ» is a question only about what is worshipped, so the norm would be for them to say: "idols", like His saying, the Exalted, وَيَسْئَلُونَكَ ماذا يُنْفِقُونَ قُلِ الْعَفْوَ، ماذا قالَ رَبُّكُمْ قالُوا الْحَقَّ، ماذا أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ قالُوا خَيْراً. But these came with the full story of their affair, like people delighted and boastful about it, so it included more than the answer to Ibrāhīm. Do you not see how they conjoined to their saying نعبد the words «فَنَظَلُّ لَها عاكِفِينَ», and did not confine themselves to the addition of نعبد alone?
An example is that you say to some rogue: "What do you wear in your town?" and he says: "I wear the Aṭḥamī cloak (a kind of cloak), and I drag its hem among the girls of the neighbourhood." And they said "we continue (nazallu)" only because they worshipped them by day and not by night. And this is the merit of elaboration: it increases the wording beyond the meaning, for an intended benefit or a sought purpose; and if there is no benefit in the increase of the wording, then it is wearisome prolixity.

safi-cedvel:72-73.t:
* I'rab:
(هل) a particle of question (إذ) an adverb of past time, attached to (يسمعونكم) «[Note: the verbs (يسمعون، تدعون، ينفعون، يضرّون) are imperfect in form and past in meaning.]», (أو) a conjunction in both places.
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «يسمعونكم ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech «[Note: in the speech there is an implied muḍāf, that is: "Do they hear your supplication", or an implied circumstantial clause, that is: "Do they hear you while you call?"]».
And the clause: «تدعون ... » is in the position of a genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «ينفعونكم ... » is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause يسمعونكم.
And the clause: «يضرّون ... » is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to the clause يسمعونكم «[Note: the object of the verb يضرّون is omitted for the verse ending, that is يضرّونكم.]».

safi-cedvel:74-74.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for a transitional rejection (iḍrāb intiqālī) (كذلك) attached to an omitted absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) whose governor is يفعلون «[Note: or attached to (يفعلون).]».
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «وجدنا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive ... and the content of speech is implied, that is: "We did not find them so."
And the clause: «يفعلون ... » is in the position of an accusative, a second object (mafʿūl bihi) whose governor is وجدنا.

safi-cedvel:75-82.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for a question (الفاء) a conjunction (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, a direct object (mafʿūl bihi).
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «رأيتم ... » is in the position of an accusative; conjoined to an implied clause that is the content of speech, that is: "Did you reflect and see ..."
And the clause: «كنتم تعبدون» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause: «تعبدون» is in the position of an accusative; the khabar of كنتم.
(76) (أنتم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, emphasis (tawkīd) for the agent pronoun in (تعبدون), (الواو) a conjunction (آباؤكم) conjoined to the agent pronoun in (تعبدون).
(77) (الفاء) resumptive «[Note: or giving the cause, if the verb of seeing is interpreted as "inform me", that is: inform me about what you worship, whether they are worthy of worship, for they are an enemy ...]», (لي) attached to an adjective of عدو (إلّا) a particle of exception (ربّ) the excepted, accusative, as a discontinuous exception «[Note: or a continuous one, according to the interpretation of their belief about the object of worship, whether Allah was among what they worship or not.]».
And the clause: «إنّهم عدوّ ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive within the scope of the preceding speech.
(78) (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, an adjective of ربّ العالمين «[Note: or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause هو يهدين, with the fāʾ redundant ... or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو".]», and the nūn in (خلقني) is for protection (wiqāya), and likewise in the verbs (يهدين، يطعمني، يسقين، يشفين، يميتني، يحيين), (الفاء) a conjunction ... and the yāʾ was dropped from the verbs for the verse endings.
And the clause: «خلقني ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «هو يهدين ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «يهدين ... » is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو).
(79) (الواو) a conjunction (الذي) a relative conjoined to the first الذي, and likewise the two relatives that follow..
And the clause: «هو يطعمني ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «يطعمني ... » is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو).
And the clause: «يسقين ... » is in the position of a nominative; conjoined to the clause يطعمني (80) (الواو) a conjunction (الفاء) connecting the apodosis ...
And the clause: «مرضت ... » is in the position of a genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «هو يشفين» has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «يشفين» is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (هو).
(81) And the clause: «يميتني ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the third relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «يحيين» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause يميتني.
(82) (أن) a maṣdar and accusative particle (لي) attached to (يغفر), (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يغفر).
And the clause: «أطمع» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the fourth relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «يغفر» ... has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the interpreted maṣdar «أن يغفر ... » is in the position of a genitive through an omitted preposition, attached to (أطمع), that is أطمع بأن يغفر.

* Rhetoric:
1- Allusion (taʿrīḍ): in His saying, the Exalted: فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِي إِلَّا رَبَّ الْعالَمِينَ.
He said «عَدُوٌّ لِي» only to picture the matter in his own self, in the sense: "I thought about my affair and saw that my worship of them is worship of an enemy, so I avoided it and preferred the worship of the One from whom all good comes." And thereby he showed them that it is advice he first gave to himself, and on which he built the planning of his affair, so that they would reflect and say: "Ibrāhīm advised us only with what he advised himself with, and wanted for us only what he wanted for his own soul", so that it would be more likely to move them to acceptance and more urgent for listening to him. Had he said: "They are an enemy to you", it would not have been of that standing, because he entered by a door of allusion, and allusion may reach the one being advised in a way that explicit statement does not reach, for he reflects on it, and perhaps reflection leads him to acceptance. Among this is what is related of al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man confronted him with something and he said:
"If you were where I am, you would need good manners."
2- The secrets of the conjunction particles: Here is a place of subtle path and delicate aim, which hardly anyone notices or any writer perceives, for most people put the conjunction particles in places other than theirs, so they govern with «في» what should be governed with «على»; just as they conjoin without noticing the secret of the particle by which the speech is conjoined. Allah the Exalted said:
«وَالَّذِي هُوَ يُطْعِمُنِي وَيَسْقِينِ، وَإِذا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ، وَالَّذِي يُمِيتُنِي ثُمَّ يُحْيِينِ». The first He conjoined with the wāw, which is for mere joining, and putting the feeding before the giving to drink, or the giving to drink before the feeding, would be permissible were it not for observing the beauty of composition. Then He conjoined the second with the fāʾ, because healing follows illness with no time empty of either; then He conjoined the third with ثم, because giving life comes after death with an interval, and for this reason ثم, which is for delay, was used in conjoining it.
3- Tankīt (the subtle point): in His saying, the Exalted, وَإِذا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ – the secret in attributing the illness to himself is good manners towards Allah the Exalted by assigning to Him alone the attribution of healing, which is an evident blessing, since he ascribed to Allah all acts of good and ascribed the act of evil to himself; and to indicate that many illnesses occur through a person's negligence in his food and drink and other things.

* Benefits:
Observing the verse endings (fawāṣil):
In His saying, the Exalted: يَهْدِينِ، ويَسْقِينِ، ويَشْفِينِ، ويُحْيِينِ» – in all these verses the yāʾ of the speaker is dropped, out of regard for the verbal pattern in the rest of the verses of the sūra. And this is not the only place where the verse endings and the musical resonance of the Qur'anic composition are observed. In the Qur'an there are many places that took this direction, which has no purpose other than to affect the minds of the listeners, especially the obstinate among the polytheists of Quraysh.
And this effect occurred in many places, as history relates to us...!

safi-cedvel:83-89.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) a vocative, a muḍāf, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the implied kasra on what precedes the yāʾ, which was dropped for lightness, and the (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (لي) attached to an omitted second object (mafʿūl bihi) whose governor is هب (الواو) a conjunction (بالصالحين) attached to (ألحقني).
Clause: «ربّ ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «هب لي ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «ألحقني ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause هب ...
(84) (الواو) a conjunction (لي) attached to an omitted second object whose governor is اجعل (في الآخرين) attached to an adjective of لسان – or to a ḥāl from it –.
And the clause: «اجعل ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the response to the vocative.
(85) (الواو) a conjunction (من ورثة) attached to the second object of the verb اجعلني ...
And the clause: «اجعلني ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
(86) (الواو) a conjunction (لأبي) attached to (اغفر), (من الضالّين) attached to the khabar of كان.
And the clause: «اغفر ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «إنّه كان من الضالّين ... » has no grammatical position; giving the cause.
And the clause: «كان من الضالّين..» is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of inna.
(87) (الواو) a conjunction (لا) prohibitive, jussive, and the sign of the jussive in (تخزني) is the dropping of the weak letter.. and the (نون) is for protection (wiqāya) (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (تخزني), and the (الواو) in (يبعثون) is the deputy agent ...
And the clause: «لا تخزني ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
(88) (يوم) the second, a badal (substitute) for the first adverb, accusative (لا) negative, and the second (لا) is redundant, to emphasise the negation (بنون) conjoined with the wāw to مال, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw, so it is attached to the masculine plural.
And the clause: «لا ينفع مال ... » is in the position of a genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
(89) (إلّا) a particle of exception (من) a relative noun in the position of an accusative as a continuous exception «[Note: the excepted-from is implied in the preceding verse, that is: "the day when wealth will not benefit anyone ... except him who comes ...", and it may be discontinuous, with the excepted-from being wealth and sons ... and some of the i'rab scholars make (إلّا) mean لكن, with (من) after it a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "that benefits him" ... Furthermore the verb (أتى) came past in form and imperfect in meaning, and likewise the verbs أزلفت، برّزت، كبكبوا، قالوا ... which follow ...]», (بقلب) attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of أتى.
And the clause: «أتى ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (من).

* Morphology:
(85) ورثة: plural of وارث, an active participle from the triliteral ورث; its wazn is فاعل, and the wazn of ورثة is فعلة with two fatḥas.
(89) سليم: a sifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from the triliteral سلم, pattern of فرح; its wazn is فعيل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Advancing: in His saying, the Exalted, رَبِّ هَبْ لِي حُكْماً وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ.
He first asked to be granted judgment (ḥukm), then asked to be joined with the righteous, and the secret in it is very subtle: the theoretical faculty precedes the practical faculty, because one can know the truth even if he does not act on it, while the reverse is not possible; for knowledge is an attribute of the spirit and action is an attribute of the body, and just as the spirit is nobler than the body, so knowledge is better than righteousness.
2- Figurative usage (majāz): in His saying, the Exalted, وَاجْعَلْ لِي لِسانَ صِدْقٍ فِي الْآخِرِينَ.
The "tongue" is a figure for mention (dhikr), by the relation of causation, and the lām is for benefit, from which the description of being beautiful is gained.

safi-cedvel:90-93.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive «[Note: or a conjunction, conjoining the clause أزلفت to the clause لا ينفع ... in the position of a genitive.]», (الجنّة) the deputy agent, nominative (للمتّقين) attached to (أزلفت).
Clause: «أزلفت الجنّة ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
(91) (الواو) a conjunction (الجحيم للغاوين) like الجنّة للمتّقين.
And the clause: «برّزت الجحيم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أزلفت.
(92) (الواو) a conjunction (لهم) attached to (قيل), (أين) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, an adverb of place attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما), and the returning pronoun is omitted, that is "you worshipped them" ...
And the clause: «قيل ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أزلفت.
And the clause: «أين ما كنتم ... » is in the position of a nominative; the deputy agent «[Note: it is originally the content of speech of the active verb.]».
And the clause: «كنتم تعبدون» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause: «تعبدون..» is in the position of an accusative; the khabar of كنتم.
(93) (من دون) attached to a ḥāl from the implied returning pronoun (هل) a particle of question, for denial and mockery (أو) a conjunction.
And the clause: «ينصرونكم» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «ينتصرون ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause ينصرونكم.

safi-cedvel:94-95.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive, and the wāw in (كبكبوا) is the deputy agent (فيها) attached to (كبكبوا) by including in it the meaning of "they were cast on their faces" (هم) a pronoun in the position of a nominative, emphasis (tawkīd) for the attached pronoun, the deputy agent (الغاوون) conjoined to the pronoun that is the deputy agent, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
Clause: «كبكبوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
(95) (الواو) a conjunction (جنود) conjoined to the attached pronoun that is the deputy agent (أجمعون) emphasis (tawkīd) for the conjoined words, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.

* Rhetoric:
The strength of the word for the strength of the meaning: in His saying, the Exalted, فَكُبْكِبُوا فِيها هُمْ وَالْغاوُونَ.
This is among the things in which Ibn Jinnī is unique, in the book «al-Khaṣāʾiṣ», for kabkaba is the repetition of kabba (to cast down).
He made repetition in the word an indication of repetition in the meaning, as if, when one is cast into Jahannam, he is thrown down time after time until he settles in its depths.

safi-cedvel:96-102.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) (فيها) attached to (يختصمون).
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «هم فيها يختصمون» is in the position of an accusative; a ḥāl from the agent of قالوا.
(97) (التاء) the tāʾ of the oath (الله) the name of majesty, genitive through the (التاء), attached to an implied verb أقسم (إن) the lightened form of the heavy one (inna), inoperative, (اللام) is the distinguishing one (al-lām al-fāriqa) «[Note: and it is a substitute for the lām of the oath that is obligatory in the khabar of inna.]», (في ضلال) attached to the khabar of كنّا.
And the clause: « (أقسم) بالله» is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: «إن كنّا لفي ضلال ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the oath.
(98) (إذ) an adverb of past time, attached to the "being" (istiqrār) to which the khabar of كنّا is attached «[Note: it is not attached to the maṣdar ضلال because it is a description before it has acted ... some permit the attachment, some imply an omitted verb, that is "we went astray when we made you equal", and some attach it to مبين, that is "we were in the utmost manifest error at the time of our making you equal to the Lord ..."]», (بربّ) attached to (نسوّيكم).
And the clause: «نسوّيكم ... » is in the position of a genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
(99) (الواو) parenthetical (ما) negative (إلّا) a particle of restriction (المجرمون) the agent of أضلّنا, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
And the clause: «ما أضلّنا إلّا المجرمون» has no grammatical position; parenthetical.
(100) (الفاء) a conjunction (ما) negative (لنا) attached to a fronted khabar (شافعين) genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ.
And the clause: «ما لنا من شافعين» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath.
(101-102) (الواو) a conjunction (لا) redundant, to emphasise the negation (صديق) conjoined to شافعين, genitive like it in form. (الفاء) resumptive (لو) a particle of wishing (لنا) attached to the khabar of أنّ (كرّة) the ism of أنّ, postponed, accusative (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation (نكون) an incomplete imperfect verb, accusative through an implied أن after the fāʾ, and the ism of نكون is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "نحن" (من المؤمنين) the khabar of نكون.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لنا كرّة) is in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is "if our return were achieved".
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن نكون ... ) is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the maṣdar كرّة, that is: "would that we had a return, so that we would be believers".
And the clause: «لو رجوعنا (حاصل) » has no grammatical position; resumptive within the scope of the saying.
And the clause: «نكون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن), which is implied.

* Morphology:
(شافعين) plural of شافع, an active participle from the triliteral (شفع); its wazn is فاعل.
(حميم) a sifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from حمّ الأمر فلانا, meaning "the matter concerned so-and-so", pattern of نصر; and al-ḥamīm is the close one whose affair concerns you, or the friend; its wazn is فعيل.

* Rhetoric:
Clarification (īḍāḥ): in His saying, the Exalted, وَلا صَدِيقٍ حَمِيمٍ.
Īḍāḥ is that the speaker mentions speech in whose outward form there is some obscurity, then clarifies it in the rest of his speech; and the difficulty that īḍāḥ resolves is in the meanings of badīʿ (figures) of words and in their i'rab, and the meanings of the soul, apart from the (other) arts. It is here in His saying, the Exalted: وَلا صَدِيقٍ حَمِيمٍ, for the friend described with the attribute ḥamīm is the one who surpasses kinship and exceeds it, in that he is ḥamīm. Al-ḥamīm is from iḥtimām, which is concern, that is: our affair concerns him and his affair concerns us. It is also said to be from al-ḥāmma, which is the inner circle, from their saying "ḥāmmat so-and-so", meaning his intimates.

* Benefits:
1- The discussion of the two prepositions «wāw and tāʾ» and their being specific to the oath has already preceded, and that the tāʾ is specific to the name of majesty. We would now like to point out these two benefits:
The first is that the prepositions are divided into three kinds: «original, redundant, and resembling the redundant». a- The original: that which needs attachment and cannot be dispensed with in meaning or in i'rab.
b- The redundant: that which can be dispensed with in i'rab and needs no attached element.
c- The one resembling the redundant: that which cannot be dispensed with in wording or meaning, except that it needs no attachment, and it is five particles: «ربّ، خلا، عدا، حاشا، لعلّ».
2- A noun is made genitive in three places:
a- That it falls after a preposition.
b- That it is a muḍāf ilayhi.
c- That it follows a genitive.
Each of these three places has details that we shall take up on their occasions.

safi-cedvel:103-104.t:
* I'rab:
(في ذلك) attached to the khabar (predicate) of inna. (اللام) is for emphasis. (آية) is the postponed ism (noun) of inna, accusative. (وما كان ... الرحيم) its i'rab has already been given [Note: See verses (67, 68) of this sūra.].
The clause «إنّ في ذلك لآية ... » has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumptive clause.
And the clause «ما كان أكثرهم ... » has no grammatical position: a parenthetical clause.
And the clause «إنّ ربّك لهو ... » has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «إنّ في ذلك ... ».
And the clause «هو العزيز ... » is in the position of rafʿ (nominative) as the khabar of inna.

safi-cedvel:105-110.t:
* I'rab:
The verb in (كذّبت) is feminine in view of the meaning of the agent, which is the group or the community, not its wording, whereas the wording of «القوم» was taken into account in the words «أخوهم».
The clause «كذّبت قوم ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(106) (إذ) is an adverbial of past time attached to (كذّبت); (لهم) is attached to (قال); (نوح) is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to (أخوهم), nominative; (ألا) is a particle of offering.
And the clause «قال لهم أخوهم ... » is in the position of jarr (genitive) as muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of a genitive construct).
And the clause «ألّا تتّقون..» is in the position of naṣb (accusative) as the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).
(107) (لكم) is attached to «رسول», in the sense of «مرسل» (one sent).
And the clause «إنّي لكم رسول ... » has no grammatical position: causal.
(108) (الفاء) links the apodosis of an implied conditional, and the (النون) in (أطيعون) is the nūn of protection (wiqāya) before the yāʾ of the first person, which is omitted for the sake of the verse-ending rhyme.
And the clause «اتّقوا ... » is in the position of jazm (jussive) as the apodosis of an implied conditional, that is: "if you believe me, then fear Allah" [Note: and the implied conditional clause has no grammatical position: resumptive.].
And the clause «أطيعون ... » is conjoined to the clause «اتّقوا الله».
(109) (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is a negative particle; (عليه) is attached to «أجر» with an omitted muḍāf, that is "for conveying it"; (أجر) is genitive in form, accusative in position, a direct object, the operator being «أسألكم»; (إن) is a particle of negation; (إلّا) is for restriction; (على ربّ) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «أجري».
And the clause «ما أسألكم ... » is in the position of naṣb, conjoined to the clause of the content of the speech.
And the clause «إن أجري إلّا على ربّ ... » has no grammatical position: causal.
(110) (فاتّقوا الله وأطيعون) is like the first one, in words and clauses [Note: in verse 108 of this sūra.].

* Rhetoric:
Repetition: in the words of the Exalted «فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ» the repetition here is for emphasis and to draw attention to the fact that each of the two independently makes fear of Allah and obedience obligatory, so how much more so when they come together.

safi-cedvel:111-111.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for interrogation; (لك) is attached to (نؤمن); (الواو) is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial) ...
The clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive.
And the clause «أنؤمن لك ... » is in the position of naṣb as the content of the speech.
And the clause «اتّبعك الأرذلون ... » is in the position of naṣb as a ḥāl.

safi-cedvel:112-115.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ; (علمي) is the khabar, nominative, the sign of the rafʿ being the implied ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi; (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of jarr by the bāʾ, attached to the maṣdar «علمي», the returning pronoun being omitted, that is "they were doing it".] ...
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا يعملون) is in the position of jarr by (الباء), attached to the maṣdar «علمي».
The clause «قال ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive.
