And the clause «ما علمي ... » is in the position of naṣb, conjoined to the implied clause of the content of the speech, that is: "Are they like that, and what is my knowledge ...?"
The clause «كانوا يعملون ... » has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle (ما) [Note: the maṣdar particle, called "the literal relative" (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī)].
And the clause «يعملون» is in the position of naṣb as the khabar of kāna.
(113) (إن) is negative; (إلّا) is for restriction; (على ربّي) is attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ «حسابهم»; (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle ...
And the clause «إن حسابهم إلّا على ربّي» has no grammatical position: a resumptive within the scope of the speech.
And the clause «تشعرون ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive ... and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, that is: "you would have known that their reckoning is with my Lord".
(114) (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is negative, operating like «ليس»; (أنا) is a detached pronoun in the position of rafʿ as the ism of (ما); (طارد) is genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of (ما); (المؤمنين) is muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the jarr being the yāʾ.
And the clause «ما أنا بطارد ... » has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «إن حسابهم ... ».
(115) (إن) is a particle of negation; (أنا) is a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ; (إلّا) is for restriction; (نذير) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative.
And the clause «إن أنا إلّا نذير» has no grammatical position: causal.

safi-cedvel:116-116.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa); (إن) is a jussive conditional particle; (لم) is a particle of negation; (تنته) is an imperfect verb, jussive, the protasis; (اللام) is the lām of the oath; (تكوننّ) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of rafʿ; (من المرجومين) is attached to the khabar of «تكوننّ».
The clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive.
And the clause «لم تنته ... » is in the position of naṣb as the content of the speech.
And the vocative clause «يا نوح» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
And the clause «تكوننّ ... » has no grammatical position: the answer of the oath ... and the apodosis of the conditional is omitted, indicated by the answer of the oath.

* Morphology:
(تنته) contains an ʿilāl (weak-letter change) by omission, to suit the jussive ...
Its wazn is تفتع.
(المرجومين) is the plural of «المرجوم», a passive participle from the triliteral «رجم»; its wazn is مفعول.

* Benefits:
In this verse an oath and a conditional come together. The earlier of the two is the oath, and since the rule says that when a conditional and an oath come together and the answer is one, the answer is considered to belong to the earlier of them, and the answer of the later one is omitted and implied, explained by the first one («إذن لتكونن» is the answer to the oath), Ibn Mālik said in his Alfiyya:
واحذف لدى اجتماع شرط وقسم ... جواب ما أخرت فهو ملتزم
(Omit, when a conditional and an oath come together, the answer of the one you put later; that is obligatory.)

safi-cedvel:117-118.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) is a muḍāf vocative, accusative, from which the vocative particle has been omitted, the sign of the naṣb being the implied fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ, which is omitted for lightness ...
and the omitted (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi; the (النون) in (كذّبون) is the nūn of protection, which came before the yāʾ of the first person, omitted for the sake of the verse-ending rhyme, and (الياء) is the direct object.
The clause «قال ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive.
And the vocative clause «ربّ وجوابه ... » is in the position of naṣb as the content of the speech [Note: or it is parenthetical with no grammatical position, brought for the sake of seeking mercy ... and the clause «إنّ قومي ... » is the content of the speech, in the position of naṣb.].
And the clause «إنّ قومي كذّبون ... » has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
And the clause «كذّبون» is in the position of rafʿ as the khabar of inna.
(118) (الفاء) is a conjunction linking the effect to the cause [Note: or it links the apodosis of an implied conditional.]; (بيني) is an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (افتح), the sign of the naṣb being the implied fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ, which is muḍāf ilayhi; (بينهم) is conjoined to «بيني» by the wāw and is attached to whatever it is attached to; (فتحا) is an accusative absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq); (الواو) is a conjunction in both places, and the (النون) in (نجّني) is the nūn of protection; (من) is a relative noun in the position of naṣb, conjoined to the first-person pronoun, the object of «نجّني»; (معي) is an accusative adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of «من»; (من المؤمنين) is attached to a ḥāl from the implied returning pronoun in the ṣila [Note: or it is a tamyīz (specification) of the relative (من).].
And the clause «افتح ... » is in the position of naṣb, conjoined to the clause of the content of the speech [Note: or it is the apodosis of an implied conditional, that is: "if you wish to help me, then open ..."].
And the clause «نجّني ... » is in the position of naṣb, conjoined to the clause «افتح».

* Morphology:
(نجّني) contains an ʿilāl by omission to suit indeclinability; its imperfect is «ينجّي», and when it was moved to the imperative it was made indeclinable on omission of the yāʾ; its wazn is فعنّي.

safi-cedvel:119-120.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is a conjunction, and likewise (الواو); (من) is a relative noun in the position of naṣb, conjoined to the third-person pronoun, the object of «أنجينا»; (معه) is like the preceding [Note: in the previous verse (118).]; (في الفلك) is attached to the omitted ṣila [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun object in «أنجيناه» and what is conjoined to it.].
The clause «أنجيناه ... » has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «قال ربّ ... » [Note: in verse (117) of this sūra.].
(120) (ثمّ) is a conjunction; (بعد) is an adverb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of naṣb, attached to (أغرقنا) ...
And the clause «أغرقنا ... » has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «أنجيناه».

* Morphology:
(المشحون) is a passive participle from the triliteral «شحن»; its wazn is مفعول.
(الباقين) is the plural of «الباقي», an active participle from the triliteral «بقي»; the wazn of «الباقين» is الفاعين. It contains an ʿilāl by omission: its origin was «الباقيين» with two yāʾs; two quiescent letters met, and one of them was omitted, namely the lām of the word.

safi-cedvel:121-122.t:
* I'rab:
The i'rab of the two verses, in words and clauses, has already been given [Note: in verses (67, 68) of this sūra.].

safi-cedvel:123-135.t:
* I'rab:
(كذّبت عاد ... ربّ العالمين) are verses whose i'rab has already been given, in words and clauses [Note: in verses (105-109) of this sūra.].
(128) (الهمزة) is for reproachful interrogation; (بكلّ) is attached to (تبنون).
And the clause «تبنون ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive.
And the clause «تعبثون ... » is in the position of naṣb as a ḥāl from the agent of «تبنون» [Note: or in the position of naṣb as an adjective of «آية», the link being implied, that is "you amuse yourselves with it".].
(129) (الواو) is a conjunction, and (تتّخذون) takes a single object, in the sense of «تبنون»; and in the meaning of (لعلّكم) there is a disagreement among the exegetes.
And the clause «تتّخذون ... » has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «تبنون».
And the clause «لعلّكم تخلدون ... » has no grammatical position: it has the force of a reason [Note: it is possible that the clause is a ḥāl, in the sense "hoping for immortality".].
And the clause «تخلدون ... » is in the position of rafʿ as the khabar of laʿalla.
(130) (الواو) is a conjunction; (جبّارين) is an accusative ḥāl from the agent of «بطشتم».
And the clause «بطشتم ... » is in the position of jarr as muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «بطشتم» (the second) has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
(131) (فاتّقوا الله وأطيعون) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (108) of this sūra.], in words and clauses.
(132) (الواو) is a conjunction; (بما) is attached to (أمدّكم), the returning pronoun being omitted.
And the clause «اتّقوا الذي.» is in the position of jazm, conjoined to the clause «اتّقوا الله».
And the clause «أمدّكم ... » has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause «تعلمون ... » has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
(133-134) (بأنعام) is attached to the second (أمدّكم); (الواو) is a conjunction in the three places.
And the clause «أمدّكم» (the second) has no grammatical position: a badal (substitute) for the first clause «أمدّكم». (135) (عليكم) is attached to (أخاف).
And the clause «إنّي أخاف ... » has no grammatical position: explanatory resumptive.
And the clause «أخاف ... » is in the position of rafʿ as the khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(128) تبنون: contains an ʿilāl by omission. Its origin was «تبنيون», with a yāʾ after the nūn; the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent and the ḍamma was transferred to the nūn (an ʿilāl by quiescence); then the yāʾ was omitted because it met the wāw of the agent while quiescent, so it became «تبنون»; its wazn is تفعون.
(ريع) is the plural of «ريعة», which is a raised place or a path opening out in a mountain; its wazn is فعل with a kasra then a sukūn.
(129) مصانع: plural of «مصنعة», which is a basin or a pool; its wazn is مفعلة with a fatḥa or a ḍamma on the mīm, and a fatḥa or a ḍamma on the lām, and it is of the type of ism al-makān (noun of place) ...
And the wazn of «مصانع» is مفاعل, with a fatḥa on the mīm and a kasra on the ʿayn ... and «المصانع» also means fortresses.

* Benefits:
1- «إذ قال لهم أخوهم هود»:
In the words of the Exalted «أخوهم هود» there is a gracious hint indicating that the messenger or prophet comes from the middle of the people to whom he is sent; he is not a tyrant from among their tyrants, nor an angel from the angels of heaven, but a servant from among the servants of Allah, whom He has chosen to deliver His message to a group of His creation; he shares with them all their human affairs and is distinguished by the revelation that comes down to him and which he is commanded to convey; so he is their brother in every case.
2- When the badal is a noun and the mubdal minhu (the noun substituted for) is an interrogative noun or a conditional noun, the badal must be preceded by the interrogative hamza or the conditional «إن», as in: كم رجالك أعشرون أم ثلاثون ("How many are your men: twenty or thirty?").
The grammarians call it badal tafṣīl (substitute of specification). It is restricted to the badal muṭābiq (identical substitute), as in: من جاءك أزيد أم عمرو ("Who came to you: Zayd or ʿAmr?"), and as in:
«من يجتهد إن علي أو خالد فأكرمه» ("Whoever strives, whether ʿAlī or Khālid, honour him"): «من» is a jussive conditional noun in the position of rafʿ, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause after it is its khabar; «إن» is a conditional particle with no operation here, because it was brought to clarify the meaning and not to operate; «علي» is a badal from the latent pronoun in «يجتهد», and «خالد» is conjoined to «علي», and the clause «فأكرمه» is in the position of jazm as the apodosis of the conditional.
And as in: حيثما تنتظر في المدرسة وإن في الدار أو إفك فتبصّر وأرجو لك الهداية إلى الصواب ("Wherever you wait, whether at school or at home or in falsehood, look carefully; and I hope guidance to the right for you.") [Translator's note: the Arabic of this last example appears corrupt in the source; it is translated as written.]

safi-cedvel:136-138.t:
* I'rab:
(سواء) is a fronted khabar, nominative; (علينا) is attached to «سواء» [Note: or to an omitted adjective of «سواء».]; (الهمزة) is a maṣdar particle of equalization; (أم) is a conjunction equivalent to the hamza; (من الواعظين) is attached to an omitted khabar of «تكن».
And the interpreted maṣdar (أوعظت ... ) is in the position of rafʿ, a postponed mubtadaʾ, that is:
"your admonishing is the same to us, or your not admonishing."
The clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive.
And the clause « (وعظك) سواء ... » is in the position of naṣb as the content of the speech.
And the clause «وعظت ... » has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the literal relative (الهمزة).
And the clause «لم تكن من الواعظين ... » has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «وعظت».
(137) (إن) is a particle of negation; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction; (خلق) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «هذا» ...
genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of «ما», and the sign of the jarr is the yāʾ. [Translator's note: the text is cut off here in the source, between the khabar of «هذا» and the end of a statement about a khabar of «ما»; it is translated as written.]
And the clause «إن هذا إلّا خلق ... » has no grammatical position: causal.
(138) (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is negative, operating like «ليس»; (معذّبين) is genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of «ما», and the sign of the jarr is the yāʾ.
And the clause «ما نحن بمعذّبين» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the causal clause.

* Morphology:
(الواعظين): plural of «الواعظ», an active participle from the triliteral «وعظ», of the chapter of «ضرب»; its wazn is فاعل.
(خلق): a noun in the sense of a person's nature and disposition; its wazn is فعل with two ḍammas.
(معذّبين): plural of «معذّب», a passive participle from the quadriliteral «عذّب»; its wazn is مفعّل, with a ḍamma on the mīm and a fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:139-140.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive, and the second is a conjunction; (إنّ في ذلك ...
العزيز الرحيم) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in words and clauses, in verses (67, 68) of this sūra.].
The clause «كذّبوه ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive.
And the clause «أهلكناهم ... » has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «كذبوه».

safi-cedvel:141-152.t:
* I'rab:
(كذّبت ثمود ... ربّ العالمين) the i'rab of its like has already been given [Note: in verses (105-109) of this sūra.], in words and clauses.
(146) (الهمزة) is for reproachful interrogation, and the (الواو) in (تتركون) is the deputy agent; (في ما) is attached to (تتركون); (هاهنا) is an indeclinable demonstrative, preceded by the particle of alerting, in the position of naṣb as an adverb of place attached to an omitted ṣila of «ما»; (آمنين) is an accusative ḥāl from the deputy agent.
And the clause «تتركون ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive within the scope of the preceding speech.
(147) (في جنّات) is attached to whatever the relative «ما» is attached to, because it is a badal from it with repetition of the preposition.
(148) And the clause «طلعها هضيم ... » is in the position of jarr as an adjective of «نخل».
(149) (من الجبال) is attached to (تنحتون), as it is made to imply the meaning of «تتّخذون» [Note: or (من) has the meaning of «في».]; (فارهين) is an accusative ḥāl from the agent of «تنحتون».
And the clause «تنحتون ... » has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «تتركون».
(150) (فاتّقوا الله وأطيعون) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (108) of the sūra.], in words and clauses ...
(151) (الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is a prohibitive, jussive particle, and the sign of the jazm in (تطيعوا) is the omission of the nūn ... and the wāw is the agent.
And the clause «لا تطيعوا ... » is conjoined to the clause «اتّقوا ...».
(152) (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of jarr, an adjective of «المسرفين»; (في الأرض) is attached to (يفسدون) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from the agent of «يفسدون».]; (لا) is negative.
And the clause «يفسدون ... » has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause «لا يصلحون ... » has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the ṣila.

* Morphology:
(148) هضيم: a derived adjective from the triliteral «هضم», of the chapter of «فرح», meaning it became fine and soft; its wazn is فعيل in the sense of مفعول.
(149) فارهين: plural of «فاره», from the triliteral «فره», meaning to be skilled and proficient, of the chapter of «كرم»; an active participle, its wazn is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Majāz (figurative usage): in the words of the Exalted «وَلا تُطِيعُوا أَمْرَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ».
Attributing obedience to the command is majāz, whereas it is literally attributed to the one who commands; and in that there is a degree of exaggeration that is not hidden. It is possible that obedience is used metaphorically for compliance, because of the resemblance between them in leading to doing what one was commanded, or that it is a majāz mursal (a figure by association) for it, because of its being inseparable from it.
Irdāf (implication): in the words of the Exalted «الَّذِينَ يُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا يُصْلِحُونَ».
Since «يفسدون» does not preclude their sometimes doing good, it was followed by the words of the Exalted «وَلا يُصْلِحُونَ» to show the perfection of their corruption and that it was never mixed with any good at all.

safi-cedvel:153-154.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) is a restricting particle and what is restricted by it (kāffa and makfūfa); (من المسحّرين) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «أنت».
The clause «قالوا..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
And the clause «أنت من المسحّرين ... » is in the position of naṣb as the content of the speech.
(154) (ما) is negative; (إلّا) is for restriction; (مثلنا) is an adjective of «بشر», nominative [Note: (مثلنا) gained no definiteness through the annexation.]; (الفاء) links the apodosis of an implied conditional; (بآية) is attached to (ائت); (كنت) is a defective past verb, a naskh verb (one that abrogates the mubtadaʾ and khabar), in the position of jazm as the protasis; (من الصادقين) is attached to the khabar of «كنت».
And the clause «ما أنت إلّا بشر ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive within the scope of the speech [Note: or a badal from the clause of the content of the speech.].
And the clause «ائت ... » is in the position of jazm as the apodosis of an implied conditional, that is: "if you are truthful, then bring a sign".
And the clause «إن كنت من الصادقين» has no grammatical position: explicative.. and the apodosis of the conditional is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

* Morphology:
(المسحّرين) is the plural of «المسحّر», a passive participle from the quadriliteral «سحّر»; its wazn is مفعّل, with a ḍamma on the mīm and a fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:155-156.t:
* I'rab:
(لها) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the first mubtadaʾ (شرب); (الواو) is a conjunction; (لكم) is like «لها», and the mubtadaʾ is the second (شرب).
The clause «قال ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive.
And the clause «هذه ناقة ... » is in the position of naṣb as the content of the speech.
And the clause «لها شرب ... » is in the position of rafʿ as an adjective of «ناقة».
And the clause «لكم شرب ... » is in the position of rafʿ, conjoined to the clause «لها شرب» [Note: and the link is implied, that is "you have a drink apart from it ... It is possible that the clause is resumptive without a link, or parenthetical."].
(156) (الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is a prohibitive, jussive particle; (بسوء) is attached to (تمسّوها), in the sense of "you inflict on it"; (الفاء) is the fāʾ of causation; (يأخذكم) is an imperfect verb put in naṣb by an implied «أن» after the fāʾ of causation; (عذاب) is the agent ...
And the clause «لا تمسّوها ... » has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumptive within the scope of the speech, that is: "do not crowd it at the time of its drinking and do not touch it ..."

* Morphology:
(شرب) is a noun for water that is drunk, or for a share of it; its wazn is فعل with a kasra then a sukūn.

safi-cedvel:157-159.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive, and the second is a conjunction.
The clause «عقروها ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive.
And the clause «أصبحوا ... » has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
(158-159) (الفاء) is a conjunction; (إنّ في ذلك ... العزيز الرحيم) the i'rab of both has already been given [Note: in verses (67, 68) of this sūra.], in words and clauses.
And the clause «أخذهم العذاب ... » has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Benefits:
- The story of Ṣāliḥ's she-camel and its hamstringing:
Al-Qurṭubī mentioned the following:
Allah revealed to Ṣāliḥ that his people would hamstring his she-camel, so he told them that, and they said: "We would never do that." Then Ṣāliḥ said to them: "In this month of yours a boy will be born who will hamstring her, and your destruction will be at his hands." They said: "No male will be born in this month but we will kill him." So nine of them had sons born in that month, and they slaughtered their sons. Then a son was born to the tenth, who refused to slaughter his son, and he had not had a son before. The tenth man's son was blue-eyed and ruddy, and he grew up quickly. Whenever he passed by the nine, they said: "If our sons were alive they would be around before this." The nine became angry with Ṣāliḥ, because he had been the cause of their killing their sons, so they banded together, or swore by Allah: "We shall attack him and his family by night." They said: "We will go out on a journey, and people will see our journey, and we will be in a cave, so that when night comes and Ṣāliḥ goes out to his mosque, we will come to him and kill him, then we will say: 'We did not witness the destruction of his family, and we are truthful,' and they will believe us and know that we had gone out on a journey." Ṣāliḥ did not sleep with them in the village, but used to sleep in the mosque, and when morning came he would go to them and admonish them.
When they entered the cave they wanted to come out, but the cave collapsed upon them and killed them. The people who had learned of this saw it, and cried out in the village: "O servants of Allah, was Ṣāliḥ not satisfied that he commanded them to kill their children until he killed them too?" So the people of the village gathered to hamstring the she-camel.
It is related that Misṭaʿ drove the she-camel into a narrow place in a mountain pass and shot her with an arrow that hit her leg, so she fell; then Qudār struck her. It was also said that he said: "I will not hamstring her until they all agree," so they would enter upon the woman in her chamber and say: "Do you agree?" and she would say: "Yes," and likewise their children.
For that reason "Qudār" became a proverb of ill omen. In this Zuhayr says:
وما الحرب إلا ما علمتم وذقتم ... وما هو عنها بالحديث المرجم
(War is nothing but what you have known and tasted, and it is not, about it, mere conjectural talk.)

متى تبعثوها تبعثوها ذميمة ... وتضر إذا ضريتموها فتضرم
(If you rouse it, you rouse it as something blameworthy, and it rages when you provoke it, and blazes up.)

فتعرككم عرك الرحى بثفالها ... وتلقح كشافا ثم تنتج فتتئم
(Then it grinds you as the millstone grinds with its grist, and it conceives repeatedly, then gives birth to twins.)

فتنتج لكم غلمان أشأم كلهم ... كأحمر عاد ثم ترضع فتفطم
(Then it bears for you boys, all of them more ill-omened than the red one of ʿĀd; then it suckles and weans.)
That is, it bears you sons, each of whom matches in ill omen the hamstringer of the she-camel, Qudār ibn Sālif. It was right for Zuhayr to say "like the red one of Thamūd", but he said "like the red one of ʿĀd". In this he missed the mark, and exalted is He who does not err. [Translator's note: this closing remark is the author's; it is translated as written.]

safi-cedvel:160-166.t:
* I'rab:
(كذّبت قوم لوط ... على ربّ العالمين) The like of these has already been parsed, in words and clauses, [Note: in verses (105-109) of this sūra.] ...
(165) (الهمزة) is for the interrogative of rebuke and reproach (من العالمين) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الذكران ...
And the clause «تأتون ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive clause.
(166) (الواو) is a conjunction (ما) is a relative noun in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (لكم) is attached to (خلق), (من أزواجكم) is attached to a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun [Note: or it is a tamyīz (specification) of the relative (ما).], (بل) is for transitional rejection (إضراب) (قوم) is a khabar (predicate), nominative (عادون) is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم, nominative ...
And the clause «تذرون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause تأتون.
And the clause «خلق لكم ربّكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause «أنتم قوم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive ...

* Morphology:
(165) الذكران: plural of الذكر, a noun for what is the opposite of the female; its pattern is فَعَل (with two fatḥas), and the pattern of الذكران is فُعْلان (with ḍamma then sukūn). There are other plurals too, namely ذكور (with ḍamma on the dhāl) and ذكارة (with kasra on the dhāl).
(166) عادون: it has a weakening by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf); its origin is عاديون, with a yāʾ before the wāw. The ḍamma was found heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made sukūn and its vowel was transferred to the dāl before it ... then it was deleted because it met the wāw as a silent letter, so عادون became of the pattern فاعون (cf. 173 - al-Baqara).

* Rhetoric:
Vagueness (al-ibhām): in His saying, the Exalted, ما خَلَقَ لَكُمْ.
By it He intended their rear passages, and in that is a regard for modesty and discretion. And «من» can be explicative and can be partitive.

safi-cedvel:167-167.t:
* I'rab:
The like of this has already been parsed, in words and clauses, [Note: in verse (116) of this sūra.]

safi-cedvel:168-169.t:
* I'rab:
(لعملكم) is attached to بالقالين [Note: The grammarians make the attachment to an omitted khabar, its implied form being «قالٍ» (with tanwīn on the lām), and (من القالين) is a naʿt of the omitted khabar, on the claim that the ṣila of the relative (ال) does not act upon what precedes the relative ...], (من القالين) is the khabar of إنّ ...
The clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «إنّي ... من القالين» is in the position of accusative, the reported speech (maqūl al-qawl).
(169) (ربّ) is the vocative, a muḍāf, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the implied fatḥa on the letter before the omitted yāʾ, omitted for lightness, and the omitted (الياء) is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and (النون) in (نجّني) is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) (أهلي) is conjoined by the wāw to the pronoun yāʾ in (نجّني), accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the implied fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) is the muḍāf ilayhi (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of genitive, with the returning pronoun omitted.].
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما يعملون) is in the position of genitive through (من), attached to (نجّني).
And the clause: «ربّ» ... has no grammatical position; it is resumptive within the scope of the speech.
And the clause: «نجّني ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «يعملون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما).

* Morphology:
(القالين), plural of القالي, an active participle from the triliteral قلى, that is, "he hated". In (القالين) there is a weakening by deletion; its origin is القاليين, with two silent yāʾs, one of which, the lām of the word, was deleted, and the sign of the case ending remained; its pattern is الفاعين.

safi-cedvel:170-175.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive (أهله) is conjoined by the wāw to the pronoun of the third person in (نجّيناه), accusative (أجمعين) is tawkīd (emphasis), accusative [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) if the maṣdar is intended by it.], and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause: «نجّيناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
(171) (إلّا) is a particle of exception (عجوزا) is accusative as the excepted (في الغابرين) is attached to a naʿt of (عجوزا).
(172) And the clause: «دمّرنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
(173) (الواو) is a conjunction (عليهم) is attached to (أمطرنا), (مطرا) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq if the maṣdar is intended by it.], (الفاء) is a conjunction (ساء) is a past verb for the construction of censure (inshāʾ al-dhamm) (مطر) is the fāʿil of the verb of censure, nominative ... and the one censured (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "مطرهم".
And the clause: «أمطرنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause دمّرنا.
And the clause: «ساء مطر المنذرين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أمطرنا.
(174-175) (إنّ في ذلك ... العزيز الرحيم) Both have already been parsed [Note: in verses (67, 68) of this sūra.]

* Benefits:
- فَساءَ مَطَرُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ:
We pointed out earlier that the verbs of praise are three: نعم, حبّ and حبذا.
And that the verbs of censure are also three, namely:
بئس, ساء, and لا حبذا.
We add to that that the sentences of these verbs are performative (inshāʾiyya) and not declarative (khabariyya). And these verbs are not conjugated, because they do not contain the meaning of the event that goes with conjugation.
- Remark: حبذا is a verb compounded of «حبّ» and «ذا», a demonstrative.
- Second remark: the tamyīz (specification) precedes the one praised or censured (al-makhṣūṣ), for example:
ألا حبذا قوما سليم فإنهم ... وفوا وتواصوا بالإعانة والصبر
(Oh, how excellent a people is Sulaym, for they were faithful and urged one another to help and to patience)
and it may come after it, as in:
حبذا الصبر شيمة لامرئ رام ... مباراة مولع بالمغاني
(How excellent is patience as a trait for a man who sought a contest, one fond of dwellings)
- Third remark: the «ذا» that is in «حبذا» stays singular and masculine even if the one praised or censured is otherwise, and five matters must be observed regarding the tamyīz of this chapter; for brevity we refer you to the longer works of grammar.
And the tamyīz may be implied in the verse we are dealing with, so we say «ساء مطرا مطر المنذرين», and other analyses are possible. So reflect and choose ...

safi-cedvel:176-184.t:
* I'rab:
(كذّب أصحاب ... على ربّ العالمين) The like of these has already been parsed, in words and clauses, [Note: in verses (105-109) of this sūra.]
(181) (الواو) is a conjunction (لا) is a prohibitive jussive particle (من المخسرين) is attached to the khabar of تكونوا.
And the clause: «أوفوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive clause [Note: or a resumptive clause within the scope of the speech.].
And the clause: «لا تكونوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أوفوا ...
(182) (الواو) is a conjunction (بالقسطاس) is attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of زنوا, that is, "being furnished with the scale".
And the clause: «زنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أوفوا..
(183) (الواو) is a conjunction (لا) is a prohibitive jussive particle (أشياءهم) is a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (لا تعثوا) is like لا تبخسوا (في الأرض) is attached to (تعثوا), (مفسدين) is an accusative ḥāl, confirming the meaning of its governing verb.
And the clause: «لا تبخسوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أوفوا ...
And the clause: «لا تعثوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أوفوا ...
(184) (الواو) is a conjunction (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi (الجبلّة) is conjoined by the wāw to the pronoun of address, the accusative object, accusative, (الأولين) is a naʿt of الجبلّة, accusative like it, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
And the clause: «اتّقوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to أوفوا ...
And the clause: «خلقكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).

* Morphology:
(المخسرين), plural of المخسر, an active participle from the quadriliteral أخسر; its pattern is مُفْعِل (with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn).
(الجبلّة), a noun meaning the creatures and nations, taken from الجبل (the mountain) because of their strength; its pattern is فِعِلّة (with kasra on the fāʾ and the ʿayn and a shaddated fatḥa on the lām), and there are other dialectal forms of its pronunciation.

* Benefits:
الأيكة has two readings: a- الأيكة: which is the tangled trees or the thicket.
b- ليكة: which is the name of the village in which the people of Shuʿayb lived.
Accordingly, regarding الأيكة, which is the thicket or the trees tangled one with another, we mention some of what the poets said about the الأيك and its cooing dove on its branches. One of them said:
أيبكي حمام الأيك من فقد إلفه ... وأصبر عنها إنني لصبور
(Does the dove of the thicket weep at the loss of its mate while I endure without her? I am indeed enduring)
And al-Riyāshī recited for one of them:
دعوت فوق أفنان من الأيك موهنا ... مطوقة ورقاء في إثر آلف
(I called, above the branches of the thicket in the dead of night, a collared grey dove after a mate)

فهاجت عقابيل الهوى إذ ترنمت ... وشبت ضرام الشوق تحت الشراسف
(She stirred the remnants of passion when she warbled, and kindled the blaze of longing beneath the rib-ends)

بكت بجفون دمعها غير ذارف ... وأغرت جفوني بالدموع الذوارف
(She wept with eyelids whose tears did not flow, and incited my eyelids to flowing tears)
And ʿAwf ibn Muḥallim said:
ألا يا حمام الأيك إلفك حاضر ... وغصنك ميّاد ففيم تنوح
(O dove of the thicket, your mate is present and your branch is swaying, so why do you lament?)

أفق لا تنح من غير شيء فإنني ... بكيت زمانا والفؤاد صحيح
(Wake up, do not lament for nothing, for I wept a time while the heart was sound)

ولوعا فشطت غربة دار زينب ... فها أنا أبكي والفؤاد جريح
(In passion, then the far exile of Zaynab's abode departed; so here I am weeping while the heart is wounded)

safi-cedvel:185-187.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا إنّما ... المسحّرين) These have already been parsed, in words and clauses, [Note: in verse (153) of this sūra.], (ما أنت ... مثلنا) has already been parsed [Note: in verse (154) of this sūra.]. (إن) is the lightened form of the heavy (inna), made inoperative [Note: When the lightened (إن) enters a verbal sentence, and the verb is a nāsikh (one that abrogates the nominal sentence), it must be left inoperative.], (اللام) is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa) (من الكاذبين) is attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi governed by نظنّك.
And the clause: «إن نظنّك لمن الكاذبين» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause of the reported speech.
(187) (الفاء) links the apodosis of an implied condition (علينا) is attached to (أسقط), (من السماء) is attached to a naʿt of (كسفا), (إن كنت من الصادقين) has already been parsed [Note: in verse (154) of this sūra.].
And the clause: «أسقط ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, that is:
"if you are truthful, then make fall".
And the clause: «كنت من الصادقين ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative ... and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

safi-cedvel:188-188.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: and a relative noun in the position of genitive, with the returning pronoun omitted, that is, تعملونه.]. And the interpreted maṣdar (ما تعملون) is in the position of genitive through the bāʾ, attached to (أعلم).
The clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive clause.
And the clause: «ربّي أعلم ... » is in the position of accusative, the reported speech.
And the clause: «تعملون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما).

safi-cedvel:189-191.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive, and the second is a conjunction, and the ism of (كان) is a latent pronoun referring to "the punishment of the Day of the Shadow (يوم الظلّة)" ...
And the clause: «كذّبوه ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «أخذهم عذاب ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «إنّه كان عذاب ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive clause.
(إنّ في ذلك ... العزيز الرحيم) Both have already been parsed, in words and clauses, [Note: in verses (67, 68) of this sūra.]

safi-cedvel:192-199.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis ...
And the pronoun in (إنّه) refers to the Noble Qur'an.
The clause: «إنّه لتنزيل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
(193) (به) is attached to a ḥāl from الروح, that is, "furnished with it", and the governing element in it is نزل ...
And the clause: «نزل به الروح ... » is in the position of nominative, a second khabar of (إنّ) [Note: or it has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumptive clause.].
(194-195) (على قلبك) is attached to (نزل), (اللام) is causal (تكون) is a defective imperfect verb, a nāsikh, accusative through an implied أن after the lām (من المنذرين) is attached to the khabar of تكون (بلسان) is attached to (نزل) [Note: or attached to المنذرين ... and al-ʿUkbarī permitted making it a badal (substitute) of (به) by repeating the preposition, that is, "speaking in the Arabic language".], (مبين) is a second naʿt of لسان, genitive.
And the interpreted maṣdar أن تكون is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to (نزل).
And the clause: «تكون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied maṣdar particle (أن).
(196) (الواو) is a conjunction (اللام) is the shifted lām, for emphasis (في زبر) is attached to the khabar of إنّ.
And the clause: «إنّه لفي زبر..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إنّه لتنزيل ...
(197) (الهمزة) is for the interrogative of reproof and reproach (الواو) is a conjunction (لهم) is attached to a ḥāl from آية (آية) is the khabar of يكن, accusative (أن) is a maṣdar and subjunctive particle ...
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يعلمه علماء ... ) is in the position of nominative, the ism of يكن.
And the clause: «لم يكن ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إنّه لفي زبر.
And the clause: «يعلمه علماء ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (أن).
(198) (الواو) is a conjunction (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle, "impossibility of the second because of impossibility of the first" (imtināʿ li-imtināʿ) (على بعض) is attached to (نزّلناه) ...
And the clause: «لو نزّلناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لم يكن لهم آية.
(199) (الفاء) is a conjunction (عليهم) is attached to (قرأه), (ما) is a negative particle (به) is attached to مؤمنين, the khabar.
And the clause: «قرأه عليهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause نزّلناه.
And the clause: «ما كانوا به مؤمنين» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of the non-jussive conditional (لو).

* Morphology:
(192) تنزيل: a maṣdar with the meaning of the passive participle, that is, "that which is sent down"; its pattern is تفعيل.
(195) عربيّ: a relational noun (ism mansūb) ascribed to عرب, a collective generic noun (ism jins jamʿī); its pattern is فَعَلِيّ (with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the ʿayn).
(198) الأعجمين: plural of الأعجم, which is a shortened form of الأعجميّ (with the yāʾ of relation), a noun for one who does not speak Arabic; it is an adjective of the pattern أفعل and its feminine is عجماء, and the regular plural of it would be عجم (with ḍamma then sukūn), but it was given the sound plural of a plural in view of its origin in the relational form; and it is from عجم يعجم of the chapter كرم, meaning that there was a thickness (lukna) in his tongue.

safi-cedvel:200-203.t:
* I'rab:
(كذلك) is attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq governed by سلكناه, and the pronoun of the third person in the verb refers to the Noble Qur'an with an omitted muḍāf, that is: "we made its denial enter" (في قلوب) is attached to (سلكناه).
The clause: «سلكناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
(201) (لا) is a negative particle (به) is attached to (يؤمنون), (حتّى) is a particle of limit and genitive (يروا) is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive through an implied أن after حتّى.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يروا ... ) is in the position of genitive through (حتّى), attached to the negated (يؤمنون).
And the clause: «لا يؤمنون ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from المجرمين or from the hāʾ.
And the clause: «يروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied maṣdar particle (أن).
(202) (الفاء) is a conjunction (يأتيهم) is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive, conjoined to (يروا), (بغتة) is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar because it coincides with it in meaning, that is, "it surprises them with a surprise", or it is its kind, that is, "the coming of surprise".], that is: "taking by surprise" (الواو) is the wāw of ḥāl (لا) is a negative particle ...
And the clause: «يأتيهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يروا.
And the clause: «هم لا يشعرون ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl.
And the clause: «لا يشعرون» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
(203) (الفاء) is a conjunction (يقولوا) is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive, conjoined to يأتيهم, and the sign of the subjunctive is the deletion of the nūn ... and the (الواو) is the fāʿil (هل) is an interrogative particle with the meaning of regret or of hoping for the impossible ...
And the clause: «يقولوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يأتيهم.
And the clause: «هل نحن منظرون ... » is in the position of accusative, the reported speech.

* Benefits:
- Conditions of the sound masculine plural (jamʿ al-mudhakkar al-sālim):
Three conditions are required for it:
a- That the feminine tāʾ not be attached to it. So this plural is not formed from nouns such as طلحة, nor from adjectives such as علّامة, lest the two signs, of feminine and masculine, which are contradictory, be combined in them..
b- That it be for a masculine. So this plural is not formed from the proper name of a female, such as زينب, nor from the adjective of a female, such as حائض.
c- That it be rational, because this plural is specific to rational beings. So it is not formed from «شوشو» as a name of a dog, nor «سابق» as an adjective of a horse; and that it not be a compound by blending (tarkīb mazjī) nor a predicative compound (tarkīb isnādī). There are some further details which we have passed over for the sake of brevity and out of regard for the plan of the book.

safi-cedvel:204-204.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for the interrogative of reproof (الفاء) is a conjunction (بعذابنا) is attached to (يستعجلون).
The clause: «يستعجلون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, that is:
"Are they heedless of their condition, of asking for a respite, so that they seek to hasten our punishment?"

safi-cedvel:205-207.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for the interrogative (الفاء) is resumptive (متّعناهم) is a past verb, indeclinable, in the position of jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) (سنين) is an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (متّعناهم), and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ, since it is joined to the sound masculine plural.
The clause: «رأيت ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «متّعناهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical ... and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the interrogative that follows, that is: "their enjoyment did not avail them ..."
(206) (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative, fāʿil of جاءهم [Note: and it is also the mafʿūl of رأيت, by way of mutual contention (tanāzuʿ).], and the (الواو) in (يوعدون) is the nāʾib fāʿil.
And the clause: «جاءهم ما كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause متّعناهم.
And the clause: «كانوا يوعدون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause: «يوعدون ... » is in the position of accusative, the khabar of كانوا, and the returning pronoun is omitted.
(207) (ما), the first, is an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi governed by أغنى, and it is for denial and negation [Note: this is when it indicates a thing; and it is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq if it indicates a maṣdar with the meaning of "availing" (al-ighnāʾ).], (عنهم) is attached to (أغنى), (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of nominative, as fāʿil, with the returning pronoun omitted, that is, يمتّعونه.] and the wāw in (يمتّعون) is the nāʾib fāʿil.
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا ... ) is in the position of nominative, fāʿil of أغنى ...
And the clause: «أغنى ... » is in the position of accusative, the second mafʿūl bihi of the verb رأيت in the sense of "tell me".
And the clause: «كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما).
And the clause: «يمتّعون ... » is in the position of accusative, the khabar of كانوا.

safi-cedvel:208-209.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive (ما) is a negative particle (قرية) is genitive in form and accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi (إلّا) is for restriction (لها) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (منذرون).
The clause: «ما أهلكنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «لها منذرون ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from قرية, or a naʿt of it. (209) (ذكرى) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi governed by منذرون [Note: it is permissible that it be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هذه ذكرى", and the sentence is then parenthetical.], (الواو) is a conjunction, or of ḥāl (ما) is a negative particle.
And the clause: «ما كنّا ظالمين» is conjoined to the clause لها منذرون, or is a ḥāl from the pronoun in (لها).

safi-cedvel:210-212.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive (ما) is a negative particle (به) is attached to (تنزّلت) [Note: and the pronoun in (به) refers to the Noble Qur'an.].
The clause: «ما تنزّلت به الشياطين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
(211) (الواو) is a conjunction (ما) is a negative particle, and the fāʿil of (ينبغي) is a latent pronoun referring to the Book of Allah, the Wise, that is, "it is not what they seek and desire" (لهم) is attached to (ينبغي), (الواو) is a conjunction (ما) is like the first.
And the clause: «ما ينبغي ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «ما يستطيعون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
(212) (عن السمع) is attached to (معزولون), (اللام) is the shifted lām, for emphasis.
And the clause: «إنّهم ... لمعزولون ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.

* Morphology:
(معزولون), plural of معزول, a passive participle from the triliteral عزل; its pattern is مفعول.

safi-cedvel:213-220.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive (لا) is a prohibitive jussive particle (مع) is an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted ḥāl from (إلها), and (آخر) is barred from tanwīn because it is an adjective of the pattern أفعل (الفاء) is the fāʾ of causation (تكون) is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive through an implied أن after the fāʾ (من المعذّبين) is attached to an omitted khabar of تكون.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تكون ... ) is in the position of nominative, conjoined to a maṣdar taken from the preceding prohibition, that is: "Let there be no calling on your part to the worship of another god, with the result that punishment befalls you."
The clause: «لا تدع ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «تكون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied maṣdar particle (أن).
(214-215) (الواو) is a conjunction in both places (لمن) is attached to (خفض), (من المؤمنين) is attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of اتّبعك.
And the clause: «أنذر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لا تدع.
And the clause: «اخفض ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لا تدع ...
And the clause: «اتّبعك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).
(216) (الفاء) is a conjunction (عصوك) is a past verb, indeclinable on the implied ḍamma on the omitted alif (omitted because of the meeting of two silent letters), in the position of jussive, the protasis ... and the (الواو) is the fāʿil, and the (الكاف) is the mafʿūl bihi (الفاء), the second, links the apodosis of the condition (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of genitive, with the returning pronoun omitted, that is, تعملونه.].
And the clause: «إن عصوك ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «قل ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis of the condition, accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause: «إنّي بريء ... » is in the position of accusative, the reported speech.
And the clause: «تعملون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما).
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما تعملون ... ) is in the position of genitive through (من), attached to بريء.
(217) (الواو) is a conjunction (على العزيز) is attached to (توكّل).
And the clause: «توكّل ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أنذر ...
(218) (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of genitive, a second naʿt of العزيز (حين) is an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يراك).
And the clause: «يراك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «تقوم ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
(219-220) (الواو) is a conjunction (تقلّبك) is conjoined to the pronoun of the object in (يراك), accusative (في الساجدين) is attached to the maṣdar تقلّبك [Note: and (في) has the meaning of "with", or it is attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun of address in (تقلّبك), that is, "prostrating among those who prostrate".], (هو) is a detached pronoun in the position of accusative, tawkīd of the attached pronoun, the ism of إنّ, by way of metaphor [Note: or a detached pronoun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (السميع), and the sentence is the khabar of إنّ.].
And the clause: «إنّه هو السميع ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.

* Benefits:
وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الْأَقْرَبِينَ:
When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called his relatives to the house of his uncle Abū Ṭālib, and they were forty men, give or take one.
He said: "O sons of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, if I told you that a cavalry at the foot of this mountain wished to raid you, would you believe me?" «or as he said» They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment ..."
And in one narration he said: "O sons of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, O sons of Hāshim, O sons of ʿAbd Manāf, ransom yourselves from the Fire, for I cannot avail you anything ... !"
The narrations differ, but all of them come out of one niche of light ... !

safi-cedvel:221-223.t:
* I'rab:
(هل) is an interrogative particle (على من) is attached to (تنزّل) because it is an interrogative noun, which has the right to the head of the clause, and one of the two tāʾs of the verb تنزّل has been dropped.
The clause: «أنبّئكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «تنزّل ... » is in the position of accusative; it takes the place of the second and third mafʿūl of أنبّئكم. The verb has been suspended (ta'līq) by the interrogative.
(222) (على كلّ) is attached to the second (تنزّل) (أثيم) is a naʿt of أفاك, genitive.
And the clause: «تنزّل (the second)» is in the position of accusative, a badal of the first (تنزّل).
(223) And the pronoun in (يلقون) either refers to الشياطين, or to كلّ أفّاك according to its meaning, and likewise the pronoun in (أكثرهم), (الواو) is a conjunction ...
And the clause: «يلقون ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from الشياطين, or in the position of genitive, a naʿt of كلّ أفّاك, depending on the referent of the pronoun [Note: it is permissible that the clause be resumptive, in which case it has no position.].
And the clause: «أكثرهم كاذبون ... » is conjoined to the clause يلقون, having a position or not having one.

* Morphology:
(أفاك), an intensive form from the triliteral أفك of the chapter ضرب; its pattern is فَعّال (with fatḥa on the fāʾ and shadda on the ʿayn); plural: أفّاكون.

safi-cedvel:224-227.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive, and the sentence has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «يتّبعهم الغاوون ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الشعراء).
(225) (الهمزة) is an interrogative particle, and the sign of the jussive in (تر) is the deletion of the weak letter (في كلّ) is attached to (يهيمون) [Note: it is permissible that it be attached to an omitted khabar, and the clause يهيمون a ḥāl from the pronoun in the khabar, or a second khabar.].
And the clause: «لم تر ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive clause.
And the clause: «يهيمون ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of أنّ ...

* Morphology:
(الشعراء), plural of شاعر, an active participle from the triliteral شعر, "he composed poetry"; its pattern is فاعل and the plural is فعلاء.

* Rhetoric:
Representation (al-tamthīl): in His saying, the Exalted, أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِي كُلِّ وادٍ يَهِيمُونَ.
The mention of the valley and of wandering: in it is a representation of their going into every path of speech, their straying and their little care, through exaggeration in speech and overstepping the bounds of moderation in it, until they rank the most cowardly of men above ʿAntara, and the most miserly above Ḥātim, and slander the innocent and brand the pious as sinful.

* Benefits:
1- Poetry and Islam:
Many people understood this verse wrongly, and reckoned that poetry is forbidden altogether and that the poets are all astray. This is a deficient understanding, deviating from the truth and the reality. Is poetry anything but speech, in which the good and praiseworthy occurs, and the middling and ordinary occurs? It is like ordinary speech, which is described as neither good nor bad, and in which the obscene and indecent occurs, or pure evil. This is bad, and its speaker is a wrongdoer, and we cannot take him out of the import and content of the verse.
Then, did the Messenger not have poets who defended him and Islam, and did he ﷺ not urge them and exhort them to compose poetry as a struggle for the religion and a defence of the believers?
And did he not listen to Ḥassān and others reciting their poetry in his mosque and in his presence ﷺ?
And did he not listen to Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr as he recited to him his famous ode: بانت سعاد فقلبي اليوم متبول (Suʿād has departed, and my heart today is smitten), and pardon him after his blood had been declared forfeit?
Indeed he bestowed upon him his mantle (burda), which Muʿāwiya later bought from him for thirty thousand dirhams. And the caliphs after him adopted it as an emblem which they wore on festivals and at ceremonies.
It is known of the Rightly-Guided Caliphs that they composed verse, though rarely. And the best poet among them was ʿAlī.
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say, "Indeed some poetry is wisdom ..!"
Poetry leapt a gigantic leap under the Islamic caliphate. The flourishing Islamic eras bequeathed to us an elite of poets who could not have excelled so, had the Islamic Sharia stood against poetry and pursued poets.
And the occurrence of the exception at the end of the verse إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ وَذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيراً وَانْتَصَرُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ ما ظُلِمُوا etc. makes the censure of the poets confined to the poets of the polytheists who harmed the Messenger and harmed the religion.
2- Saṭīḥ al-Ghassānī:
The first soothsayer among the Arabs; his body used to be rolled up as a garment is rolled up, and he was always lying flat on the ground. He lived (150) years and died on the night in which the Messenger ﷺ was born. He warned of the flood of al-ʿArim before it occurred.
The king of the Persians sent a messenger to him asking about a dream he had seen, and the miracles that occurred on the night of the birth of the Messenger ﷺ.
Saṭīḥ informed him, saying: "When the recitation appears, and the valley of al-Samāwa overflows, and the man of the staff appears, then Syria will not be Syria for Saṭīḥ; kings and queens of them will rule, as many as the battlements that fell, and all that is coming will come" «and Allah knows best».
